articles.title: World Cup 2026 in numbers: Key statistical goals, titles and age records
articles.summary: The 2026 World Cup has already set records for the most host nations, most matches and the highest prize money.
articles.body:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup has already set records for being the grandest tournament to date – most host nations, most matches and organisers’ claims of record attendance.

For the first time in history, three nations will be hosting the global showpiece – Canada, Mexico and the United States – across 16 cities, catering to 104 matches. The tournament features an expanded 48-team format, up from 32 in previous iterations.

FIFA has repeatedly claimed that the “cumulative attendance record of 3.5 million” set at the 1994 edition of the World Cup, also hosted by the US, is on course to be surpassed during this year’s competition, though slow ticket sales suggest otherwise.

As fans await a new chapter of history to be written at the tournament, Al Jazeera Sport takes a look at key statistics from the World Cup through the years.

⚽️ Brazil (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002)

Brazil dominate with five World Cup wins and are the only team to feature at all editions of the tournament since 1930. Altogether, the Canarinhas have appeared in seven finals and 11 semifinals .

Germany and Italy are tied for four titles each, with only the former standing a chance to gain another this year after the Azzurri missed a third consecutive World Cup.

On an individual level, none other than Brazilian legend Pele holds the record for most World Cup wins in a career (1958, 1962, 1970). Teammates Bellini and Castilho joined him for the 1958 and 1962 editions, while Cafu helped Brazil lift the trophy in 1994 and 2002.

Which player has scored the most World Cup goals ever?

The German holds the lone distinction with 16 goals across four World Cups in 24 matches.

Ronaldo (Brazil) – 15 goals in 19 matches across four World Cups

Gerd Muller (West Germany) – 14 goals in 13 matches across two World Cups

Just Fontaine (France) – 13 goals in six matches in one World Cup

Lionel Messi (Argentina) – 13 goals in 26 matches across five World Cups

Kylian Mbappe (France) – 12 goals in 14 matches across two World Cups

Pele (Brazil) – 12 goals in 14 matches across four World Cups

Which player has scored the most goals at a single World Cup?

The Frenchman scored a whopping 13 goals in six games at the 1958 World Cup in Sweden.

Sandor Kocsis (Hungary), 1954 World Cup – 11 goals

Gerd Muller (West Germany), 1970 World Cup – 10 goals

Ademir (Brazil), 1950 World Cup – 9 goals

Eusebio (Portugal), 1966 World Cup – 9 goals

Guillermo Stabile (Argentina), 1930 World Cup – 8 goals

Ronaldo (Brazil), 2002 World Cup – 8 goals

Kylian Mbappe (France), 2022 World Cup – 8 goals

Who is the youngest player at the 2026 World Cup?

⚽️ Gilberto Mora (17 years and 240 days at tournament opener on June 11)

In January 2025, Mora was the youngest to make his senior international debut for Mexico, aged 16. In August 2024, he was the youngest to start and score in the Mexican first division at age 15.

There are 22 players aged below 20 years at the tournament.

Who is the oldest player at the 2026 World Cup?

⚽️ Craig Gordon (43 years and 162 days at tournament opener on June 11)

This will be Gordon’s World Cup debut after his first international cap in 2004. The all-time record is still held by Egypt goalkeeper Essam El Hadary, who was 45 when he played at the 2018 World Cup.

There are a total of seven players aged 40 or above.

Cristiano Ronaldo (Portugal), 41 years – Sixth World Cup appearance

Guillermo Ochoa (Mexico), 40 years – Sixth World Cup appearance

Manuel Neuer (Germany), 40 years – Fifth World Cup appearance

Luka Modric (Croatia), 40 years – Fifth World Cup appearance

Lionel Messi (Argentina), 38 years – Sixth World Cup appearance

⚽️ Four (Cape Verde, Uzbekistan, Jordan and Curacao)

This is the largest number of teams to mark their World Cup entrance since 2006, when eight teams debuted.

A total of 891 players are participating in their first World Cup.

Ronaldo became the first billionaire footballer with a net worth of $1.4bn, according to Forbes, which continually ranks him in the list of the world’s highest-paid athletes owing to brand endorsements and a lucrative contract with Saudi club Al-Nassr.

Which player has the most World Cup participations?

The Argentinian icon has played 26 matches across five tournaments (2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, 2022).

Just beneath him sit Germany’s Lothar Matthaus and Klose with 25 and 24 appearances, respectively. Italy’s Paolo Maldini has 23 appearances at the World Cup, followed by Cristiano Ronaldo with 22.

⚽️ Ivory Coast is set to be the youngest squad with an average age of 25.48 years.

⚽️ Colombia. Average age of 29.98 years.

What is the least number of domestically based players in a team?

⚽️ Cabo Verde, DR Congo, Ivory Coast, Curacao, Senegal and Uruguay draw their entire squads from overseas leagues.

In contrast, Qatar and Saudi Arabia field 25 of their 26 players domestically.

What is the highest prize money for a World Cup?

FIFA announced in December a record World Cup prize fund of $727m , with the winning team taking home $50m and each team receiving ⁠⁠at least $10.5m.

It is a significant jump from the $440m prize pot in the previous edition, in which Argentina took home $42m along with the champions’ trophy.

Which is the smallest qualifying nation?

Debutants Curacao are the smallest nation at the 2026 World Cup and the smallest-ever nation to qualify.

How many nationalities are being represented?

Football’s global nature will be on full display with 71 nationalities:

Which club is most represented at the World Cup?

The Premier League club leads the list, followed by:

Paris Saint-Germain and Arsenal (16 players each)

Manchester United, Crystal Palace, Atletico Madrid, Al Hilal (12 players each)

The FIFA World Cup begins on June 11. You can follow the action on Al Jazeera’s dedicated World Cup 2026 page with all the latest news, match build-up and live text commentary, and keep up to date with group standings, real-time match results and schedules.

articles.title: "White towels with brown stains" - Giannis Antetokounmpo reveals ugly truth about Heat's visiting locker room
articles.summary: Giannis is happy he no longer has to visit the Heat's visiting locker room.
articles.body:
Giannis Antetokounmpo has been to the Miami Heat 's visiting locker room plenty of times with the Milwaukee Bucks . Today, he's happy he won't have to step inside it again, describing the conditions opposing players face when visiting the Heat .

"The visiting locker room, it's hot! No AC! The towels are old, the showers don't work. They give us white towels with brown stains!" he said.

Antetokounmpo will now experience Miami from the other side. But the biggest adjustment for him will obviously be basketball-related.

After more than a decade in Milwaukee, where he became an NBA champion, two-time MVP and one of the league's most dominant players, Antetokounmpo is beginning an entirely new chapter, coming off an injury-riddled season during which he averaged 27.6 points, 9.8 rebounds and 5.4 assists.

He has seen the Heat's arena from the visitors' perspective, dealt with everything that came with playing there and now gets to experience the organization as its biggest star.

He's also heard the stories about Pat Riley, the Heat culture, and Erik Spoelstra's coaching brilliance. Now he'll have the opportunity to experience all of these firsthand.

Regardless of what happens and how his first season with the Heat goes, at least Antetokounmpo won't have to wonder whether the visiting locker room has working showers anymore.

articles.title: Indiana RB Turbo Richard Avoids Major Leg Injury, Could Play vs. Rutgers
articles.summary: Injured running back Turbo Richard could return to the field for No. 6 Indiana this weekend when the Hoosiers visit Rutgers, meaning the defending national champions could have their top two running backs available for their first road trip this season.
articles.body: Injured running back Turbo Richard could return to the field for No. 6 Indiana this weekend when the Hoosiers visit Rutgers. If he does, the defending national champions will have their top two running backs available for their first road trip this season. Coach Curt Cignetti made the announcement Monday during his weekly news conference. "We got really good news on Turbo, and he'll be day to day, and I'm optimistic he can play Saturday as well as Rolijah Hardy," Cignetti said. Richard was injured on a 2-yard run during the second quarter of Friday night's closer-than-expected 29-23 victory over Northwestern. He was driven out of bounds and was tackled by a Wildcats player whose body came down on Richard's lower right leg near the Hoosiers' bench. No penalty was called, but Richard did not return to the game. "We'll see," was all Cignetti said about Richard during his postgame news conference. Richard transferred to Indiana from Boston College earlier this year and was the Hoosiers' top rusher until getting hurt. He has 50 carries, 383 yards and four touchdowns as well as two catches for 43 yards. Lee Beebe Jr., Richard's replacement, rushed 24 times for 203 yards and one score and set up Indiana's game-sealing TD with a 70-yard run. Beebe now leads the team with 71 carries and 398 yards and has three rushing TDs after missing all but three games in last season's Big Ten and national championship runs because of a right knee injury. The prognosis on Richard was even more critical because the other running back in Cignetti's three-runner rotation, Khobie Martin, remains out with a broken arm. Cignetti did not provide an update Monday on Martin's status, but he is expected back in the next few weeks. That meant Beebe was — and still may be — poised to carry a heavier workload. "It’s not that much pressure," Beebe said after the game. "I just know I need to step up and be there for the team. I was able to do that (Saturday). It wasn’t just me, it was the offensive line, receivers blocking downfield and it was great to mesh with (quarterback) Josh (Hoover), so it was an all-team effort." The Hoosiers (4-0, 1-0 Big Ten) also got good news on Hardy, a play-making linebacker who is tied for the team lead with 18 tackles, eight coming against Northwestern before he left the game in the second half with an undisclosed injury. Instead of going to the bench, Hardy walked straight to the locker room and did not return to the game. "We expect him to be fine," Cignetti said when asked about Hardy's playing status. Indiana has the Football Bowl Subdivision's longest active winning streak, a school-record 20 consecutive games, and the FBS' longest active home winning streak at 19. The Hoosiers also have won 12 consecutive conference games. Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: Jim Crane: Astros’ Playoff Run Will Factor Into Decision On Joe Espada's Future
articles.summary: Houston Astros owner Jim Crane said Monday the team’s playoff berth will be “something to consider" when deciding on the future of manager Joe Espada, whose contract expires after the season.
articles.body: Houston Astros owner Jim Crane said Monday the team's playoff berth will be "something to consider" when deciding on the future of manager Joe Espada, whose contract expires after the season. Crane said there have been no discussions about the possibility of a new deal for Espada recently and they’ll sit down and talk about things when the season is over. As for whether Houston winning the AL West to reach the postseason after missing out last year would have any bearing on the decision, Crane had this to say: "All positives are positives," he told The Associated Press. "All negatives are negatives. So I think that would be something to consider when we make the decision." Espada's future with the team remains in question after the Astros parted ways with general manager Dana Brown last month. Crane doesn't believe the move had an impact on how the club finished the season. "I don’t think it had a lot to do with what happened, you know, whether we won or we lost," he said. "It was a courtesy actually to give him some time because we weren’t going to renew his contract. I made a decision that we weren’t going to renew his contract, so I wanted to give him time to regroup and we knew we had enough coverage from the other three guys." After Brown's departure on Aug. 24, assistant general managers Charles Cook, Gavin Dickey and Connor Huff, along with senior adviser Jeff Bagwell, took over his responsibilities. There have been questions about how things have worked after the unorthodox move to part ways with a general manager while a team was in playoff contention. "I guess they’re working pretty good — we got into the playoffs," Crane said with a laugh. "I think everything’s fine. We’ve got a number of assistant general managers filling in, and so our communication is good. Everything’s running smooth, ready for a win." The Astros became the first team in MLB history to make the postseason without a winning record by finishing 81-81 to outlast the Texas Rangers and move on to the Wild Card Series. They'll host the Chicago White Sox in a best-of-three matchup beginning Tuesday. The Astros are in the playoffs for the ninth time in 10 years, a remarkable stretch in which they reached the ALCS seven straight times from 2017-23 and advanced to the World Series four times, winning championships in 2017 and 2022. "We’ve always said we’re here to win and we’re here to make the playoffs and make a deep run in the playoffs, and we’ve done that consistently," Crane said. "So getting in the playoffs is a big deal. If you don’t, you don’t have a chance." Reporting by the Associated Press.

articles.title: The Case Keenum Game: 3 Takeaways From Bears' Culture-Defining Win vs. Eagles
articles.summary: With Caleb Williams out, Case Keenum delivered, and then some, in the Bears' win over the Eagles.
articles.body: With Caleb Williams out, the Chicago Bears needed Case Keenum to provide a steady presence in their Monday matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Keenum delivered, and then some. Keenum, who entered the season as the Bears' third-string quarterback and hadn't started a game since 2023, played nearly flawless football. He completed 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and two touchdowns to go with a rushing score, leading the Bears to a decisive 27-7 victory. Here are my takeaways from the Monday night matchup that Chicago fans will forever know as the Case Keenum Game: 1.The Legend Of Ben Johnson Grows With Keenum's Success Monday night brought a new challenge for Ben Johnson’s reputation as a top offensive mind: Can he pull off a big win with a backup quarterback? Taking the field without Caleb Williams for the first time, Johnson’s answer, a 38-year-old Case Keenum in his first NFL snaps since 2023, was a resounding yes. Chicago’s defense helped out with three takeaways, but Keenum earned the win himself, throwing for touchdown passes to Luther Burden and Kalif Raymond against an Eagles team that came into the game 2-0. The Bears had already seen highs and lows offensively, scoring 59 points in an opening win over Carolina before a three-point showing in a rainy slog of a loss to Minnesota. For Keenum, the journeyman now has a cool piece of NFL history, joining Ryan Fitzpatrick as the only quarterbacks to start and win games with seven different NFL teams. For Keenum, that covers the Texans, the Rams (in both St. Louis and Los Angeles), the Vikings, the Broncos, the Commanders, the Browns and now the Bears. For the Bears and Johnson, they continue to keep pace in a talented NFC North, behind the surprising 3-0 Vikings and even at 2-1 with the Lions. Chicago stays home to face the Jets on Sunday before a biggest test at Green Bay in Week 5. 2.The NFC East Race Is Closer Than You Think With the Eagles' loss, they fell into a tie with the New York Giants at 2-1 atop the NFC East, on a day that New York traded a fifth-round pick to acquire quarterback J.J. McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings. The Washington Commanders got their first win Sunday, upsetting the Seattle Seahawks, and the Dallas Cowboys are 1-2 with the highest-scoring offense (and defense) in the division. Philadelphia’s offensive woes continued on Monday, though. The Eagles mustered only seven points against a Bears defense that gave up 37 two weeks ago to Carolina. Jalen Hurts threw for just 153 yards on 25 attempts, and Saquon Barkley rushed for 82 but couldn’t get into the end zone for a third game in a row. What’s more, the Eagles’ next two games are at home against the Los Angeles Rams and Jacksonville Jaguars – neither an easy opponent – while the Giants host the Cardinals and go to the Commanders, so it’s reasonable to think the Giants could be alone atop the NFC East entering Week 6. The Giants and Eagles play in Philadelphia in Week 9 and then close the regular season against each other at MetLife in Week 18, with plenty of division games for Washington and Dallas to get involved as well. 3. That Last Yard Is The Hardest The first half had two and nearly three drives that got to the 1-yard line but did not result in any points. First, the Bears thought they had a Colston Loveland touchdown, but after review, he was ruled down inside the 1-yard line. D’Andre Swift was dropped for a 2-yard loss, Case Keenum threw an incomplete pass and the Bears went for it on fourth-and-goal, with Keenum’s pass broken up by Eagles cornerback Quinyon Mitchell. The drive that followed was even tougher, with the Eagles also driving to the 1-yard line. Jalen Hurts was hit hard as he went out of bounds and was pulled for the game to check for a concussion. While he was out, Saquon Barkley ran to the 1-yard line, and again, the drive stalled. Barkley was dropped for a 1-yard loss, and on third-and-goal from the 2, backup Andy Dalton was intercepted in the end zone by rookie safety Dillon Thieneman. The Eagles nearly did it again just before halftime. With no timeouts and 11 seconds left, Hurts threw a pass to DeVonta Smith, but he was stopped at the 1. With the final seconds ticking off, the Eagles quickly lined up and got the snap off in the final second, with Hurts diving in for a touchdown. Had he attempted to spike the ball to stop the clock, it didn’t look like he’d have done it in time. And just like the Eagles, the Bears avenged their previous 1-yard line shortcoming when Keenum scored a 1-yard QB sneak that extended the Bears' lead to 27-7. How rare is it for an NFL team to drive 90-plus yards and not score? There were 81 drives of 90 yards and longer last year, and only five of them failed to yield points: 74 touchdowns, two field goals, three interceptions, one fumble and one turnover on downs. It’s worth noting that two of those came against Chicago: one field goal and a Dak Prescott interception for Dallas. Before Monday, the Eagles’ last 11 drives of 90-plus yards had all resulted in touchdowns.

articles.title: Phil Taylor to come out of retirement and reunite with Adrian Lewis
articles.summary: Phil Taylor will come out of retirement to play in the Modus Super Series alongside Adrian Lewis in November.
articles.body:
Sixteen-time world champion Phil Taylor will return to darts eight years after retiring to play in the Modus Super Series' International Pairs tournament in November.

Taylor will play alongside another former world champion, Adrian Lewis, who himself has not played professionally on the PDC circuit since April 2023.

Taylor, 66, is the most-decorated player in the sport's history. 'The Power' won 214 professional tournaments and a record 87 major tournaments between 1987 and 2018.

The doubles tournament takes place between 23 and 28 November in Portsmouth.

Nicknamed 'Jackpot', 41-year-old Lewis won the World Darts Championship in 2011 and 2012 and has faced Taylor in five Professional Darts Corporation major title finals, all of which were won by Taylor.

The duo are the most successful pairing in the history of the PDC's World Cup of Darts, winning it four times as Team England in their six outings together.

"I've been asked plenty of times about coming back, but it would have to be for the right reason," said Taylor.

"Adrian is one of the very few people I'd come out of retirement to play alongside, and the Modus Super Series is the place I wanted to do it.

"We've got a lot of history together, we know each other's games inside out and I'm looking forward to getting back up there with him."

While Taylor has not played professionally since 2018, he did feature at the World Seniors Darts Championship in 2022, 2023 and 2024.

Lewis featured at Modus' International Pairs Tournament for England last year alongside Steve Beaton, having announced he was taking a break from darts in April 2023.

"Phil and I have shared some brilliant moments playing together over the years, so to get the chance to do it again is really special," said Lewis.

"We know what it takes to win as a pair and I'm looking forward to seeing what we can do together."

articles.title: Phil Taylor set to come out of retirement and team up with friend Adrian Lewis for pairs event
articles.summary: Darts great Phil Taylor will partner with long-time friend Adrian Lewis for the MODUS Super Series International Pairs Tournament; the 16-time world champion retired from the competitive circuit in 2018
articles.body:
The 16-time world champion will team up with long-time friend Adrian Lewis for the event, which will be held from November 23-28.

Taylor, now 66, retired from the competitive circuit in 2018, five years after winning his final world crown.

But he revealed the opportunity to play alongside Lewis was enough to bring him back to the oche, though this return is unlikely to be a permanent comeback.

Taylor, who has been practising in a pub of late and has a new dartboard in his home, said: "I've been asked plenty of times about coming back, but it would have to be for the right reason.

"Adrian is one of the very few people I'd come out of retirement to play alongside, and the MODUS Super Series is the place I wanted to do it.

"We've got a lot of history together, we know each other's games inside out, and I'm looking forward to getting back up there with him."

Taylor, who recently underwent a successful hip replacement, and Lewis previously teamed up to win four World Cup of Darts titles.

"Phil and I have shared some brilliant moments playing together over the years," Lewis said.

"So to get the chance to do it again is really special.

"We know what it takes to win as a pair and I'm looking forward to seeing what we can do together."

The MODUS Super Series is not an official PDC event but is set to host an exciting line-up of international players. The full entry list will be revealed on October 10.

articles.title: Graeme Dott: Ex-snooker world champion jailed for seven years for child sex abuse
articles.summary: Warning: This article may be upsetting, offensive and triggering to some readers. This article contains details of child sexual abuse; Graeme Dott appeared at the High Court in Edinburgh on Tuesday, where he was sentenced to seven years in jail
articles.body:
The 49-year-old subjected a girl and a boy to multiple incidents of abuse, with the girl targeted between 1993 and 1996 and the boy between 2006 and 2010.

Dott appeared at the High Court in Edinburgh on Tuesday, where judge Lord Harrower told him he had "robbed the complainers of a significant part of their childhood".

Imposing a backdated sentence of seven years, he said Dott's behaviour had involved a "gross violation of trust".

A five-day trial heard Dott exposed himself in front of both children, touched them inappropriately and kissed them.

In August, he was found guilty of two counts of lewd, indecent and libidinous behaviour towards them.

During the trial, jurors heard from one of Dott's victims, a woman now in her 40s.

She told the court that Dott had sexually abused her on multiple separate occasions while she was a child.

The second victim, a man who is now in his late 20s, said he was sexually abused by Dott on multiple occasions.

Dott had denied the charges but was found guilty by the jury.

Lord Harrower remanded him in custody and his name was added to the sex offenders register.

Dott, who turned professional in 1994, won the World Snooker Championship in 2006, defeating Peter Ebdon in the final at the Crucible in Sheffield.

He reached the final in two other years but was beaten by Ronnie O'Sullivan in 2004 and Neil Robertson in 2010.

Following his conviction, Dott's name was removed from World Snooker's Hall of Fame.

articles.title: 6 NHL Players Likely to Be Traded After the Kirill Marchenko-Matthew Knies Deal
articles.summary: After an entire offseason of speculation, Kirill Marchenko has found the new home he was looking for.
articles.body:
After an entire offseason of speculation, Kirill Marchenko has found the new home he was looking for.

Marchenko's move from Columbus to Toronto was among the NHL's most consequential late-September transactions, with the Maple Leafs acquiring the forward in a six-player trade with the Blue Jackets.

That does not necessarily mean other prominent players will move as quickly. Still, several notable names could emerge as trade candidates in the coming weeks and months.

We'll look at players seeking new teams as the new NHL season begins and consider where they could go and how soon, if at all, they might be traded.

Time isn't standing still for the Winnipeg Jets or anyone else in the NHL, but it is for Connor Hellebuyck while he waits to be traded.

The Jets added Clay Stevenson off waivers from the Washington Capitals to join Stuart Skinner in the crease. Potential suitors for Hellebuyck are still going about business as usual, even though some have had injury concerns arise.

Whether it's the Buffalo Sabres (Alex Lyon and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen each left preseason games early with injuries), the Utah Mammoth (Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa look set to own the net to start the year), the San Jose Sharks (Yaroslav Askarov and Alex Nedeljkovic), or the Carolina Hurricanes (Brandon Bussi and Pyotr Kochetkov), they've all made plans without Hellebuyck. Even the Edmonton Oilers, with Frederik Andersen (injured), Tristan Jarry, and Devon Levi, are ready to go.

The market for the three-time Vezina winner and 2025 MVP is there, but it's not burning up, which is bad news for Hellebuyck.

That said, with how fickle goaltending can be and how injuries can wreak havoc on a team's season should the No. 1 guy go down, all it takes is one team to push hard to bring him in and nothing scares a team into action like a bad injury or a worse start to the season.

All it takes for a player to agree to a trade is a market that's not there and a desperation to get out of an increasingly ugly situation. This is where Dylan Larkin is at.

While Larkin is dealing with an upper-body injury, he's reportedly expanded the list of teams he'd accept a trade from. His original list of Florida, Minnesota, Tampa Bay, and Vegas has been joined by Colorado, Dallas, and Washington.

All of these teams are tight to the cap ceiling, and after a report that Detroit turned down offers from Boston and Minnesota for Larkin, and with Wings management having a few fires to put out, moving Larkin remains difficult.

After all, Larkin has years left on his contract, and while he and the Red Wings have a semi-peaceable way of winding down his career in Detroit (removing the captaincy and such), should he suit up for them again, the reception at home should be icy enough to hurry along the process of moving him.

Will it be enough for him to expand his list even more, or enough for Detroit to lower their demands? Maybe we'll get to find out.

What's been fascinating about Alexander Nikishin's negotiations with Carolina is how he's managed to get his name tossed into trade scenarios alongside some of the other big targets in the league, especially Connor Hellebuyck. With Marchenko off to Toronto, that potential outlet was eliminated.

Nikishin's situation is particularly tricky, not just because he's a restricted free agent; there's also the possibility he could return to Russia and the KHL if an offer (or a team) comes along that he's unhappy with.

Being part of a Stanley Cup-winning team and performing well makes him desirable, but the contract battle hasn't settled, and that can make things tense with the season now here.

A team like the New York Rangers stepping in to acquire Nikishin would make sense if not for being one of Carolina's rivals in the Metropolitan Division.

There are plenty of other clubs that could use help on the blue line, but Nikishin's situation means teams are a bit wary in case he heads back home.

While most of the Canadiens' younger players seem to be signing long-term, team-friendly contracts, Kirby Dach has yet to sign one, which is enough to make you wonder if something is up.

Sportsnet's Frank Seravalli shared recently that Edmonton and Calgary have snooped around Dach, who is in the final year of his contract this season. Edmonton could use some depth at forward, and Calgary could use some experienced players, period. But does that mean Dach is immediately available? Not exactly, although the Canadiens have a ton of depth to work with.

After the Habs added Chris Kreider, Dach slides down the depth chart and is poised to play third-line minutes, though his hold on that spot might be tenuous, which could make ice time harder to find. With a $3.5 million cap hit, he's affordable, and if it's not the Oilers or Flames, any other team in need of an experienced forward could come calling, too.

We're trying really hard not to pick on the Detroit Red Wings, but the team has made it really hard to ignore what in the world is going on there. Case in point, as yet unsigned RFA defenseman Simon Edvinsson who skated and practiced with the team through training camp and still doesn't have a new contract.

With the season underway, Edvinsson won't be working out with the team anymore and the fact that he still hasn't signed after Shawn Horcoff was appointed interim general manager is a problem.

Detroit has plenty of cap space to work with (more than $16 million) and a desperate need to get Edvinsson back on the blue line with his partner Moritz Seider. This situation should be simple enough to settle, but if it stays stressed, there's no doubt teams will come calling for the 6'6" 222-pound defenseman.

There's been speculation for a while now about whether Seattle's Shane Wright's future is with the Kraken.

He saw his numbers drop significantly last season after a solid rookie season two years ago, and as he enters the final year of his entry-level contract, we're all wondering what is next for him.

A big season this year would quiet everyone down about Wright's future, but with teams on the lookout for help, his name occasionally comes up. Elliotte Friedman mentioned on the 32 Thoughts Podcast that the Edmonton Oilers are looking for center help and peeked at Wright, although he added that the possibility seemed unlikely.

At 22 years old and with fewer than 200 games in the NHL, there's room for him to grow and develop, but the Kraken aren't in a position to punt on any of their young top prospects, especially a player they selected fourth overall in 2022.

There's plenty of room to grow with the Kraken, and if Wright can have a true breakout season, trade talk will end for good. Until then, though, teams around the league will believe they can add him and turn things around.

articles.title: B/R NHL Staff Predictions for the 2027 Stanley Cup Winner
articles.summary: And it all begins again on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The start of the 2026-27 season is finally here as the NHL expands to a new 84-game regular-season schedule. As always in the league, parity is paramount, and many teams could lift the Stanley Cup in the summer of 2027.

The B/R NHL hockey writers have provided their predictions below.

Montréal Canadiens Will Bring the Cup Back to Canada

Four years after finishing dead last in the NHL standings, the Montréal Canadiens finished sixth overall last season with 106 points and advanced to the Eastern Conference Final.

This year, the Canadiens are no longer rebuilding. Led by young superstars Nick Suzuki and Cole Caufield and rising stars Lane Hutson, Juraj Slafkovský, and Ivan Demidov, they're poised to take the next step as legitimate Stanley Cup contenders.

Goaltender Jakub Dobeš was the Canadiens' playoff hero last spring. If he can build on that, he could become a Vezina Trophy candidate. Meanwhile, Hutson, Noah Dobson, and Mike Matheson anchor the blue-line corps, with promising David Reinbacher waiting in the wings.

The Selke Trophy-winning Suzuki, 51-goal scorer Caufield, Calder Trophy runner-up Demidov, and power forward Slafkovský provide considerable firepower. The addition of Chris Kreider gives them a veteran net-front presence with considerable playoff experience.

Thanks to head coach Martin St. Louis and the shrewd management of hockey ops president Jeff Gorton and general manager Kent Hughes, the Canadiens are an emerging force in the Eastern Conference. They have what it takes to end Canada's 33-year Stanley Cup drought.

Picking the defending Stanley Cup champions to repeat is boring and suggests I might be afraid to take a stand.

The truth is that Carolina's championship in June has little to do with this belief. In fact, the irony of last season is that it wasn't even GM Eric Tulsky's attempt to go for it.

If the Hurricanes' roster stays stagnant, they are already a contender and the team to beat in the East. A lack of true star power is compensated for by the deepest roster in the NHL, one in which the players play the relentless way the 'Canes do.

They're bringing back most players from last season. Talented but often-injured Freddie Andersen has moved to Edmonton, while the fate of defenseman Alexander Nikishin hangs in the balance.

I do not expect that the Hurricanes' roster will look the same by March as it does now. In fact, the headlines could come much sooner. They have almost every critical player locked up long-term and enter the season with nearly $8.5 million in cap space.

Remarkably, Carolina also has a surplus of draft picks, including an additional 2028 first-rounder from the Rantanen trade. It is poised to make a blockbuster addition. Maybe even two. Goaltender Connor Hellebuyck is the obvious candidate. You have to wonder about Dylan Larkin as well. The Hurricanes are going to be like a shark scenting blood for any top-six center who shakes loose.

Finally, it's about the path. Teams like Colorado, Tampa, and Dallas might be just as good. Arguably, better. The Central and Metropolitan divisions are going to be a gauntlet, and all teams will have a tough time making it to the Conference Final. In comparison, the Hurricanes are best challenged in the Metropolitan by the New Jersey Devils, Washington Capitals, and New York Rangers. Three teams that could make some noise but aren't true contenders.

The Hurricanes should comfortably win the division and then be the odds-on favorite to emerge from the Metropolitan Division. From there, it's anyone's guess how it goes, but even getting that far seems a lot more likely for Carolina than for any other team in the NHL.

I can already see folks cringing at the thought of Vegas winning the Stanley Cup again.

The reality is that every team in professional sports should want to do what the Golden Knights intend to do every season: win the championship. No long rebuilds, no organizational letters, none of that. To paraphrase a quote from a team that plays in the same city: Just win, baby.

Whether it's Jack Eichel or Mitch Marner, Vegas and general manager Kelly McCrimmon somehow find a way to land a big piece to improve the team. Now, that may come at a cost to their future, but championships last forever. Rebuilds just feel like they do.

It helps that the Golden Knights play in the weak Pacific Division. No one is challenging Vegas for the top spot: not Anaheim, not San Jose, not Edmonton. Sorry, folks, it's Vegas' division to lose.

With the Central being a gauntlet, Vegas will have an easy road to the Stanley Cup Final. Sure, they'll need to see more from Carter Hart in goal, but if he reverts to his poor 2026 Stanley Cup Final form, McCrimmon and Co. aren't shy about being ruthless and finding another netminder. Oh, and they still have Stanley Cup-winning goalie Adin Hill on the roster.

Don't like it? Find a team that can beat them. The smart bet here says there won't be one.

6 NHL Players Likely to Be Traded After Marchenko-Knies Deal

Oilers Finally Break Through Behind McDavid

Let's say you're forecasting the Stanley Cup winner for 2027.

You could pick Carolina. You could pick Vegas. You could pick Montréal.

And none would get you laughed out of your fan group.

Each finished in the top half of the regular-season standings in 2025-26, each was in the final four come playoff time, and the Hurricanes wound up hoisting the Cup.

No one will be (or should be) surprised if any of them are parading next summer.

But I'm more of an off-the-board guy when it comes to predictions. I'm saying it will be the Edmonton Oilers.

Full disclosure: I've been an Oilers fan since I was in single digits. My now-teenage son is named after Ryan Smyth and Wayne Gretzky. And I attended games in the since-abandoned mecca once known as the Northlands Coliseum.

So, if you're suggesting it's a "homer" pick, you have a leg to stand on.

Lest we forget, the Oilers have the league's best player in Connor McDavid. They have one of their elite snipers (and playmakers) in Leon Draisaitl. And they have a point-per-game defenseman in Evan Bouchard.

Any team with that sort of talent deserves to be taken seriously. Add in the focus on detail being preached by Cup-winning coach Mike Babcock, and there's plenty of reason to believe a change in mindset will get Edmonton over the hump for the first time since 1990.

All I ask when June comes is that you remember where you first heard it.

But don't worry, regardless of where you are in Canada, the U.S., or elsewhere, you'll probably hear me celebrating anyway.

Carolina Repeats as Stanley Cup Champion

It's almost always bland to say that a team that just won a title is going to go back-to-back and win it again, but when a team plays a smothering and panic-inducing style of hockey like the Carolina Hurricanes do, it just makes sense.

Carolina's brand of hockey has yet to be appropriately copied by anyone else in the league, which means there's no one else out there working on doing what it does but better.

Proven winning styles always get mimicked, and there are plenty of teams out there with elements of them. But Carolina has it down to an exact science. It won the Stanley Cup last season with a team playing a unified style and without eye-popping superstars on the roster.

Stars, yes, but a top-of-the-bill star of the sport? No, and that's just fine because it means they can roll four lines to make opponents wish they were playing anyone else in the league.

With defenders like Jaccob Slavin and K'Andre Miller, forwards like Sebastian Aho and Nikolaj Ehlers, and goalies Brandon Bussi and Pyotr Kochetkov holding it down, there's no reason to think the Hurricanes won't run it back again.

They'll face a stiffer challenge within the Metropolitan Division from the Washington Capitals, while the team that emerges from the bruising Atlantic Division could be worn down by the time it reaches the Eastern Conference Final—just as the Montréal Canadiens were last season.

Although Vegas tested them in the Final last season, the Hurricanes were too strong and will be again this season.

articles.title: NHL Power Rankings for Opening Night of the 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Merry Christmas, hockey fans.
articles.body:
Exactly 107 days since the Carolina Hurricanes skated the Stanley Cup around the ice at T-Mobile Arena, 10 of the NHL's 32 teams will begin their quests to be the last one standing when the 2026-27 season comes to an end next summer.

Five games make up Tuesday's Opening Night schedule, with puck drops in Raleigh, Toronto, Boston, Edmonton, and Las Vegas.

B/R's hockey staff tempered its giddiness just long enough to contemplate a set of Power Rankings just in time for the new season's arrival.

Take a look at what we came up with and drop a thought in the app comments.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | UTA | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

The good news for Manny Malhotra? He's a head coach in the NHL. The bad news? He's the head coach of the Canucks, who are widely expected to have the worst record in the league at the end of 2026-27.

The "Battle of Alberta" games will be fun, and Dustin Wolf is on his way to becoming a homegrown stud in the net. But beyond fleeting reasons for interest and optimism, it'll probably be a long season in Calgary.

Let's face it. There hasn't been a lot to be excited about when it comes to the Kraken since they went for 100 points and made the playoffs in the franchise's second season. Chances are it won't be happening this season either.

6 NHL Players Likely to Be Traded After Marchenko-Knies Deal

Connor Bedard isn't the only young stud on the Chicago roster, but he's the one who matters the most. This makes it even more concerning that coach Jeff Blashill said Bedard isn't close to practicing after a summertime injury.

It's not just old guys. But there may not be enough young guys on the Nashville roster to make the Predators viable in the Central. Mavrik Bourque, 24, went from 11 to 20 goals in two full seasons in Dallas and arrived via trade in July.

The Blues were near the bottom of the league in offense last season, averaging 2.80 goals, but they do have emerging young skill players. That puts the onus on Joel Hofer, who started 43 games last season, to be a reliable No. 1 in net.

Adding a few more teams to his "yeah, I'd play there" list makes it more likely that a trade-requesting Dylan Larkin's zip code will soon change. But whether he stays or goes, it's not likely to do much to get the Red Wings past a decade of irrelevance.

Precocious center Adam Fantilli is locked up through 2032 at $13.75 million per season, but Zach Werenski isn't. And it's the reigning Norris Trophy winner's status that will be a constant issue until he's either extended or traded.

Monday's trade swapping Kirill Marchenko for Matthew Knies salvaged a tough situation for general manager Don Waddell.

Connor Hellebuyck's status has cast uncertainty over Winnipeg's season. After he failed to report to training camp and was suspended by the club, his future with the Jets appears uncertain amid ongoing trade speculation .

If he is unavailable, Winnipeg will face a significant challenge in recapturing the form that made it a Presidents' Trophy contender.

Matthew Schaefer is a bona fide star, but there's not too much to get excited about beyond him. The only player on the team to exceed 60 points in 2025-26, Mathew Barzal, is not guaranteed to play on opening night thanks to a left knee issue.

Here's a question. Are the Kings, as currently constituted, good enough to compete in the Pacific Division and the West as a whole? Artemi Panarin is a star, but only one player (Adrian Kempe) on the team for all of 2025-26 exceeded 50 points.

The Bruins put the over in overachievement last season, registering 100 points during the regular season before going seven games with Buffalo in the playoffs. But let's face it. There's not a lot in the cupboard beyond new captain David Pastrnak.

There are many possibilities in New York. The Rangers could miss the playoffs for the third straight time since winning a Presidents' Trophy. Or, newcomer Pavel Dorofeyev could be the impact player he's been in the preseason. Stay tuned.

It certainly doesn't help Ottawa's prospects for 2026-27 that its most impactful player in 2025-26, Brady Tkachuk, is now playing in Florida. Can Linus Ullmark (.891 save percentage last season) return to his All-Star and Vezina-caliber form from 2022-23?

Like the Rangers, the Maple Leafs have a variety of possible results for the 2026-27 season. If Auston Matthews rediscovers his 60-goal form and Sergei Bobrovsky is what he was in Florida's playoff runs, it'll be a fun year in hockey-mad Toronto.

Yes, the Penguins were a 98-point team in 2025-26. But can they be that good again, without any major additions? Pittsburgh scored the third-most goals in the league last season, but there's no goalie on the roster who's a proven starter.

Many teams would envy that the Devils don't have a rostered goalie making $2 million. Then again, the trio of Jake Allen, Nico Daws and Remi Poirier doesn't inspire confidence. Perhaps a healthy Jack Hughes can net 50 on the other end.

The Ducks got to the playoffs and took down the two-time defending Western champs in the opening round, but their blue line took an offseason hit, and keeping Leo Carlsson (at $18 million annually) didn't help the salary structure.

We'll also file the Flyers in the "were they really a 98-point team last season?" column. There is some young talent in Matvei Michkov, 21, and Porter Martone, 19, but unless they make a prolonged impact in 2026-27, it figures to be a regression.

Are the Sharks the Ducks of 2026-27? Given 10 forwards and four defensemen younger than 30, it's not a bad bet. Macklin Celebrini, 20, was named captain, and both Michael Misa, 19, and Ivar Stenberg, 18, were noticeable in the preseason.

The franchise that was starving for a playoff berth finally got one after 14 seasons, and now the focus shifts to a first Cup. It may not come in 2026-27, but the Sabres are young enough and good enough to be title-relevant for years to come.

Look at the rosters around the league, and you would be hard-pressed to find a team with more young, productive, and now NHL-proven talent than the Mammoth.

They're in tough in a loaded Central, but who would want to play them in April?

Well, you can say a lot of things about the Capitals, but you can't say they're just standing pat with Alex Ovechkin. Washington signed both Boone Jenner (from Columbus) and traded for Alex Tuch (from Buffalo) on the first day of free agency.

Edmonton enters the season under intense scrutiny following its decision to hire Mike Babcock. The Oilers were sharp in the preseason, and a more disciplined approach on the blue line and in net could materially raise their ceiling in the standings.

Make no mistake: the most persistent questions will be about Quinn Hughes until he either moves or decides to extend his stay in Minnesota. But any team with Kirill Kaprizov and Matt Boldy in its top-six forward group is capable of big things.

It's a weird situation in Vegas, where Ryan Craig heads behind the bench with a team that made a Cup Final appearance with an interim coach after firing its coach in late March and beating the West's No. 9 team by just nine points. Which is reality?

From 2020 to 2022, it was a foregone conclusion that the Lightning would reach the Cup Finals, which they did three straight times, hoisting the Cup twice. Now, after four straight first-round exits, is it a foregone conclusion that they're out of the loop?

OK, the Stars would love to win a Central title and set up an easier April run. But ask a Dallas fan if regular-season items mean anything after three straight losses in the West Final and last spring's first-round flop. It's Cup Final or bust in Texas.

If the NHL had a WWE-like NXT division, the Canadiens would be its champion. Simply put, no city in the league boasts a more attractive cache of young talent. And the addition of Chris Kreider, with his 348 career goals, on the cheap was huge.

Sure, they missed the playoffs in 2025-26, so the Panthers are destined to be a non-factor in 2026-27. Don't you believe it? Adding Brady Tkachuk and Aleksander Barkov (from injury) to a veteran core makes them an instant title threat. Again.

There are regular-season monsters and playoff monsters. The Avalanche, particularly in 2025-26, were the former. Colorado earned points in 66 of 82 games and beat the NHL field by eight points, but unless it ends in the Cup Final, it's all moot.

It was the Hurricanes' Stanley Cup to lose at this time last year, and they did not lose it. Can they repeat this season? We'll see. They return a championship-winning core, and having already won the 16 games required to capture the Cup, there is no reason to think they cannot do it again.

articles.title: The Rise and Fall of WWE's Dominik 'Dirty Dom' Mysterio
articles.summary: Dominik Mysterio, once a can't-miss prospect for WWE, has lost a lot of his luster with how he's been booked in 2026.
articles.body:
Dominik Mysterio, once a can't-miss prospect for WWE, has lost a lot of his luster with how he's been booked in 2026.

A year ago, the self-professed King of the Luchadors was not only riding high as both the AAA Mega champion and intercontinental champion, but he was also being positioned prominently on Raw as the focal point of The Judgment Day.

Following his failure to qualify for the men's Money in the Bank ladder match, fans are understandably concerned that he'll continue to suffer from a serious lack of direction going forward.

Despite being without gold for the first time since WrestleMania 41, Mysterio at least has his alliance with Liv Morgan and the rest of The Judgment Day to fall back on for the foreseeable future. However, a case can be made for the group doing more to hold him back than elevating him to the next level.

As impressive as Mysterio's ascent to stardom was, his gradual fall from grace has been equally striking.

Early Exposure on WWE TV and Teaming with His Father

Dominik Mysterio's earliest appearances on WWE TV as a child during his father Rey's rivalry with Eddie Guerrero in 2005 and the important part he played in that storyline helped lay the groundwork for his eventual introduction as a full-time talent 15 years later.

His official in-ring debut against Seth Rollins at SummerSlam 2020 went about as perfectly as it could have given his level of inexperience, but he failed to further flesh out his character beyond being the son of Rey Mysterio in the months that followed.

Dom spent his entire 2021 in the tag team division with Rey and even held the WWE Tag Team Championship for a two-month stretch, but his inability to establish an identity of his own prevented him from evolving.

Rey and Dom's various tag team battles with The Bloodline, The Judgment Day and the duo of The Miz and Logan Paul kept them busy during their time together, but it wasn't until Dom severed ties with his father that he finally started to come into his own, both as an in-ring competitor and as a character.

How Joining The Judgment Day Saved His Career

The idea of Dominik Mysterio turning heel and being a successful singles star felt too far-fetched to ever truly work.

It's possible he would have fallen flat had he been on his own, but it was more a matter of him finding the right people to bring the best out of him in that role. Just joining The Judgment Day was enough to get him comfortable as a character and make a meaningful connection with the audience.

His alliance with Rhea Ripley in particular as well as his heated rivalry with Rey Mysterio heading into WrestleMania 39 saved his career. The time he spent in NXT in the latter half of 2023 also helped him hone his skills and give him the development reps he missed out on earlier in his career.

Dirty Dom spun his wheels for the first several months of 2024 before reemerging as a key player on Raw after he helped oust Damian Priest from The Judgment Day and brought Liv Morgan into the fold to replace Ripley as his main squeeze.

Being right in the middle of that months-long feud guaranteed Mysterio a recurring role on Raw and opened fans' eyes to his potential as a future top talent.

Coming Into His Own as AAA Mega and Intercontinental Champion

Dominik Mysterio eventually became so entertaining as a heel that fans started to organically cheer for him in the early months of 2025.

All signs then pointed to him breaking away from Finn Bálor and the rest of The Judgment Day as a babyface, with his Intercontinental Championship win at WrestleMania 41 being the catalyst.

While Mysterio did walk out of 'Mania with the intercontinental title, the tension teased between him and Bálor going into the event was never followed up on. Nonetheless, Mysterio was booked strong for the remainder of the year and knocked off the likes of AJ Styles, Rusev and Penta to retain the title.

He simultaneously made a splash in WWE's newly acquired promotion AAA, where the audience got behind him in a big way and led him to capturing the AAA Mega Championship that September. As a dual champion, Mysterio was at the peak of his popularity and really starting to hit his stride.

That was especially evident when he was handpicked to work with John Cena in the 17-time world champion's final premium live event match at Survivor Series.

Dirty Dom handed Cena a rare defeat (albeit with an assist from all of The Judgment Day) to regain the Intercontinental Championship and set himself up for what should have been an even bigger 2026.

Mere weeks removed from his career-defining win over John Cena at Survivor Series, Dominik Mysterio suffered a shoulder injury while wrestling at an AAA event.

It sidelined him indefinitely and brought an abrupt halt to any plans WWE had for him to start 2026, including his involvement in the men's Royal Rumble match.

Mysterio ultimately returned to television on the post-Rumble Raw to celebrate Liv Morgan's women's Royal Rumble win, but he remained a background player until after Elimination Chamber. As a result, the Intercontinental Championship became a total afterthought and wasn't defended on WWE TV for over two months.

The injury obviously wasn't something WWE planned for him, but the lack of follow-up with him once he was ready to return to the ring was definitely the fault of those in charge creatively. It was almost as if he lost his spot to some of the newer names getting called up such as Oba Femi and Je'Von Evans and was never able to bounce back.

His loss of the Intercontinental title to Penta in early March marked the beginning of his downfall. It was wise to have him get beaten for the belt instead of having him relinquish it due to his injury, but any momentum he gained from defeating Cena by that point was all but gone.

Failing in Feuds with Finn Bálor and Danhausen

Despite doing little of note in the first few months of 2026, he did make the WrestleMania card for the fifth consecutive year by taking on Finn Bálor.

The two revisited their tension from the year prior, this time with Bálor going babyface and splitting from The Judgment Day on his own terms.

Their match was given a No Disqualification stipulation shortly before showtime, which did make it more enjoyable than it may have been otherwise. They had a quality contest, but Bálor winning sent the message that WWE had bigger plans for him coming out of WrestleMania, not Mysterio.

Once that rivalry ran its course, he shifted his focus to Danhausen, who "cursed" Mysterio backstage the night he lost the Intercontinental Championship to Penta. That program was a waste of Mysterio's entire summer and culminated in an abysmal "Human Monies on a Pole" match between the two at SummerSlam, which was won by Danhausen.

That was in addition to him not having won a match that mattered almost all year. He was eliminated from the King of the Ring tournament in the semifinals, lost the AAA Mega Championship to El Grande Americano at Triplemania 34, and failed to qualify for the men's Money in the Bank ladder match.

As of this writing, Mysterio's stock is as cold as it's been in years, but that isn't to say he can't turn his luck around on the sooner side.

Why He'd Benefit From Hitting the Reset Button Completely

There's no doubt Dominik Mysterio still generates great heat any time he has a microphone in his hand, but without a stable direction, fans aren't going to view him as anything other than the average midcarder.

With the work he's put into improving as a wrestler and creating his character, it'd be a big step backward for WWE to continue utilizing him as a stepping stone the way they have been.

The Money in the Bank briefcase would have been the perfect gimmick to keep him busy until cashing in down the card, but now WWE must seek alternate routes with Mysterio.

There will come a time when he embraces the audience as a babyface, but that shouldn't and doesn't necessarily need to happen in the near future. He can instead take the time to reestablish himself, get back in the win column and reclaim his spot as The Judgment Day's de facto leader.

The alliance with Liv Morgan has been mutually beneficial so far and should continue for as long as they remain a mildly interesting act. It would make the most sense for them to target real-life couple Becky Lynch and Seth Rollins at some point, which would get Mysterio back in the spotlight where he belongs.

Dirty Dom appeared to have a limited ceiling when he formally debuted for WWE in 2020, and now it's unfathomable that the company would cool him off so considerably after a few fantastic years.

Mysterio can and should still be a world champion in WWE, but it will take him much longer to get there if WWE continues to mishandle him.

articles.title: Jaida Parker Just Had the Best WWE Debut of 2026, Bronson Reed's Monster Moment, More Raw Fallout
articles.summary: The September 28 edition of Raw on Netflix from the Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee, Wisconsin focused on the ongoing war between The Bloodline and 946.
articles.body:
The September 28 edition of WWE Raw on Netflix from the Fiserv Forum in Milwaukee focused on the ongoing war between The Bloodline and 946.

Jaida Parker arrived on Raw for the first time, revealing at the end of the night that she had aligned with Royce Keys and her NXT partners, OTM, by running over Jacob Fatu.

Bronson Reed and Oba Femi agreed to fight at Money in the Bank, and Dragon Lee pulled off a shock win over Big Cass.

Check out all the fallout from an important WWE Raw on the road to Money in the Bank.

Jaida Parker Had the Best Main Roster Debut of 2026

Raw just added another big name from NXT as Jaida Parker aligned with 946 in the fight against The Bloodline.

This is a huge spot for Parker as she is instantly working off some of the biggest names in WWE right now.

The 27-year-old was one of NXT's most popular stars near the end of her run and now appears set for a role that leans more heavily on her character work than her in-ring ability.

This is the best spot for her early on as Parker was never the best wrestler in NXT but found ways to sell her character to a variety of audiences.

She can go forward working with Bronco Nima and Lucien Price, her primary allies in NXT, as well as working alongside one of WWE's biggest rising stars in Keys.

While Oba Femi and Trick Williams have strong cases, the spotlight immediately on Parker makes this the best debut of 2026, selling her as a big deal.

The future is bright for Parker, especially if working with the best women on WWE's main roster helps her take that final step toward becoming a complete star.

Since WWE rarely runs intergender storylines, the arrival of Jaida Parker should indicate that The Bloodline will also need a female member.

The best option is the biggest name WWE could bring back right now: Naomi.

It has been more than a year since fans last saw the former women's world champion, who has kept a low profile since announcing her pregnancy and taking time to adjust to life as a new mother.

All signs point to Naomi returning to the road soon to help combat Parker, which will give Raw another big name star.

Assuming Naomi is ready to go full speed soon, she could be the perfect first rival for the newcomer before working her way back into world title contention.

Make-or-Break Moment Coming for Bronson Reed

Bronson Reed is about to compete in one of the biggest matches of his career, alongside his Crown Jewel 2025 victory over Roman Reigns.

Facing WWE's biggest rising star, Oba Femi, could be a recipe for success—or an absolute disaster.

It is all down to the presentation. Will Reed look like a threat or a chump next to The Ruler?

After multiple recent attempts to sell him as a true threat to Femi, he should at least get close to victory on his own and perhaps win thanks to The Vision.

If the presentation is rough or the match falls short, Reed could quickly fall back into the support role for Bron Breakker and Logan Paul over presenting as a monster all his own.

Dragon Lee picked up a nice win on Raw that should mean much more for the luchador in the near future.

Dragon has outperformed his status multiple times over, and it is possible his contract will be up soon with WWE.

This is not the time to keep him in the same spot. A random win over Big Cass is fine, but he needs to look like a real threat in the midcard.

WWE should be looking to sign Dragon for the long term, possibly truly committing to him as the next Rey Mysterio.

Dragon is a veteran with over a decade of experience but also still 20 years younger than Mysterio at 31 years old.

He is one of the rare luchadors who can move like The Master of the 619 and has started to build a crowd reaction that can match what Mysterio once was.

Of all the great luchadors in WWE right now, Dragon feels the best poised to deliver in the classic lucha libre role at the top level for the next decade.

Why Are We Back to Part-Time Roman Reigns?

When Roman Reigns won the World Heavyweight Championship at WrestleMania 42, he said that he was done playing part-timer.

Apparently, that only extended to SummerSlam as The Tribal Chief has barely appeared since.

His match with Penta in Mexico City was fantastic but lacked a strong story beyond the luchador rising the ranks through a tournament he was always expected to win.

As the men's world champion in Raw, the company needs Reigns around not just to wrestle but also to sell the stories of his biggest matches.

At this point, LA Knight is building up his feud with The OTC alone, a familiar scenario for one of WWE's best mic workers.

It is a shame, though, because he and Reigns could have worked magic together. Instead, the actual lead storyline on Raw is The Bloodline vs. 946. Knight is a side mission title defense for The OTC.

Hopefully, Reigns will at least appear more after Money in the Bank as The Bloodline's rivalry with Royce Keys and OTM heads toward WarGames.

articles.title: 2026-27 Rangers Will Be Better, But Won't Be a True Contender Without Changes
articles.summary: In the 1994 movie Speed, Keanu Reeves' character is an LAPD officer tasked with defusing a bomb on a speeding bus filled with passengers. The bomb is automated to explode should the bus ever fall below 50 miles per hour on the busy streets of Los Angeles.
articles.body:
In the 1994 movie Speed, Keanu Reeves' character is an LAPD officer tasked with defusing a bomb on a speeding bus filled with passengers. The bomb is automated to explode should the bus ever fall below 50 miles per hour on the busy streets of Los Angeles.

What does this have to do with the New York Rangers? Well, we'll get there.

Rangers GM Chris Drury had been slow-rolling a total roster restructuring since 2024. Yes, there was a parade of messy departures, but tearing something down is easy; building anew is where the real work is. Until this past summer, it was a lot more tearing down than building anew.

One cannot look at the opening-night roster and deny that Drury has finally built something new. Eight of the 19 players who will play on Tuesday were not in the organization in January of 2026, and these are not nibbles around the edges.

Pavel Dorofeyev is the newest addition up front. The Russian winger is a welcome addition on numerous fronts. The 25-year-old is a much-needed injection of youth for a forward group whose key contributors sat dangerously close to 30. He is also the best pure shooter the organization has had in well over a decade (Marian Gaborik sends his regards), while also heavily tilting the ice. That's an aspect of the game that the Rangers have been losing for years.

To that end, the other forward additions fit a common aesthetic: shot suppression. Middle-six wingers Oliver Bjorkstrand and Eeli Tolvanen, as well as new fourth-line center Joe Veleno, are reputable defensive forwards who can and will eat difficult minutes while limiting opposition offensive-zone time and clogging shooting lanes.

The defense is radically transformed and is the definitive strength of what Drury has amassed. A Marcus Pettersson-Sean Durzi duo is a strong second pairing. Remember, hilariously, that the Rangers opened last season with Will Borgen and Carson Soucy in that spot. Both are strong neutral-zone defenders, and Pettersson is a defensive specialist, while Durzi can move the puck.

Braden Schneider has caught a lot of flak in the last year, but he should be much more serviceable in a third-pairing role alongside a true defensive partner in either teenage phenom Alberts Šmits or criminally underrated Matthew Robertson. From Adam Fox down to Scott Morrow, this is the best defensive group the Rangers have boasted since 2015, balanced well with offensive catalysts and physical defenders against the rush and in the defensive zone.

The Rangers are going to be "hard to play against." Not in the sense of crashing and punching, but in a more cerebral, tactical sense. This is a team with shot-stoppers up and down the lineup and the best goaltender (Igor Shesterkin) in the NHL behind them. They're going to try to make it hard for teams to enter the offensive zone and, failing that, put the puck in the net. From there, Head Coach Mike Sullivan has to hope that there is enough individual skill and power-play excellence to carry the Rangers over the finish line after 60 minutes.

Part of how the Rangers careened into a ditch is that maneuvering often lacked foresight. JT Miller trade aside, almost every big splash from Drury in the past was an ephemeral boost; Andrew Copp, Vladimir Tarasenko, and Patrick Kane all cost a first-round pick plus more, and were rentals. The plan to overpay depth players to fill an immediate hole and turn their contracts into a problem later had hamstrung their ability to make moves. The never-ending drip of prospects and draft picks out the door hollowed out the prospect pool.

One can't accuse Drury of those mistakes this time around. Already mentioned is Dorofeyev, who is signed through his prime at a fair rate. Durzi and Pettersson are bargains in the current environment at a combined $11.5 million, and both are signed beyond this season, with Pettersson's $5.5 million cap hit through 2031 a strong value even at 30 years old. The depth additions have been risk-free. Bjorkstrand, Tolvanen, and Veleno are all paid at or below their respective market value on one-year deals.

Plus, the prospect pool is replenished. At least, to a degree. Alberts Šmits is a bona fide top prospect, while Liam Greentree and Cole Beaudoin are solid B-tier prospects who are close to NHL-ready.

The assessment of Drury's work thus far has been optimistic, but let's not mistake where the Rangers are. The Athletic's model gives the Rangers a 41% chance of making the playoffs. My own accounting, which believes there is missing context that would benefit the Blueshirts' cause, would peg their odds at around 60%. They're a high-floor team, and a repeat in the NHL's bottom five seems nearly impossible, but they're still far from contender status. If the Rangers end 2027 with 98-100 points and a second-round playoff exit, they'll have hit the upper bound of realistic expectations.

How do they build beyond that? There's no easy path. The Rangers are, at minimum, a franchise center and another top-six offensive winger short of the standard. Drury burned three first-round picks this summer just to bring in Dorofeyev and Pettersson.

The Rangers' prospect pool is deep, but they lack the pieces that would entice a team to dangle a top prospect. To that point, it seems very unlikely that the Rangers will find any star power to promote from within; the best of their youngsters, like Greentree, Beaudoin, and Malcolm Spence, look more like future third-liners than first-liners.

While the Rangers have a few rising prospects (Perreault, Šmits), the team as constructed is at the arc of its potential. Adam Fox, Pavel Dorofeyev, and Alexis Lafrenière are in their primes. Igor Shesterkin, Vladislav Gavrikov, Miller, and Mika Zibanejad won't get better with age.

The Rangers Will Be Better, But Won't Be Serious Contenders

Didn't this essay start off with a '90s movie reference? Oh, right.

The first half of Speed is filled with a series of thrilling moments in which Reaves' character manages to escape tragedy. He takes control and pulls off sharp turns. He jumps a gap in a broken roadway. He steers the car to avoid any crashes. He figures out a way to refill the gas tank as it nears empty. All while maintaining a speed above 50 miles per hour. It's creative, nimble, and miraculous.

But even as the acrobatic moments aggregate, the root problem remains. The bus is rigged with a bomb and will explode if it goes under 50 mph. Reeves doesn't have a plan to solve the bus's dilemma. His efforts are geared towards avoiding immediate catastrophe and buying time in hopes of finding a permanent way out later.

The Rangers were a rotting structure on the verge of collapse. The moves Drury has made in 2026 are a successful retool of sorts. The product should be watchable this season, and they'll be competitive, maybe even making the playoffs. But the Rangers still sit in purgatory, with no clear path to immediate contention nor discernible long-term upside. Without further organizational change that makes the team's contention window evident, they'll find themselves back in dangerous territory a few years down the road.

articles.title: Fernando Alonso reveals biggest reason behind staying in F1 with Aston Martin for 2027 season
articles.summary: Fernando Alonso has decided to continue racing in Formula 1 with Aston Martin for at least one more year.
articles.body: Fernando Alonso has decided to continue racing in Formula 1 with Aston Martin for at least one more year. The 45-year-old Spaniard says the biggest reason behind his decision is simple: he still feels fast. Alonso had been considering his future throughout the 2026 season.Despite his frustration with the new hybrid-era cars, Alonso believes he still has more to offer behind the wheel. He also sees potential in Aston Martin, with Adrian Newey playing a major role in his decision. The veteran driver says he wants another chance to compete before eventually stepping away from F1.Fernando Alonso still believes he can compete at the highest levelFernando Alonso explained that his love for racing remains the biggest factor behind his decision. He has been competing in F1 since 2001 and does not feel ready to walk away while he believes he can still match the best drivers.“First, this is my life. I have this in my blood and I keep racing and I keep enjoying and this is a way of life, in a way. Probably for me the biggest, or the clearest thing to keep racing is I still feel self-confidence that I have something extra. And when I think about stepping down or taking a different role in the team or not driving the car or whatever, in a way I feel it should not be like that because I still feel as fast as anybody. So let’s have another go”, Alonso told BBC Sport.Alonso has struggled for results this season as Aston Martin have spent much of the year near the bottom of the F1 field. His most recent podium came at the 2023 Sao Paulo Grand Prix.However, Alonso insists his personal speed has not disappeared. He pointed to moments during practice when he feels he is still faster than other drivers.“When I jump in the car, in free practice, I will see some people braking late in a corner, locking up the front tyres here or there, making mistakes there. I feel that I’m OK. Or, I’m faster than them”, Alonso said.The new 2026 regulations were another major issue for Alonso. He has repeatedly criticised the new hybrid power units and the way battery management affects driving. He has described F1 as the “battery world championship” and criticised the need to charge batteries through fast corners.Still, planned changes to the power balance have given him hope. Alonso believes the move towards a 60-40 power split by 2028 could improve the driving experience.Aston Martin’s future was also crucial. The arrival of Adrian Newey has given Alonso confidence that the team can eventually challenge at the front.“Adrian was probably the biggest contributor to this. We didn’t start it right this year but things are moving in the right direction and he’s capable of changing things very quickly”, he added.For now, Alonso has committed to another season. But he has also hinted that his F1 career could continue beyond 2027.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Former world champion Billy Joe Saunders prosecuted after beer bottle attack during baby shower brawl
articles.summary: Former boxing world champion Billy Joe Saunders has avoided immediate jail time after being involved in a violent brawl at a baby shower in Warwick.
articles.body: Former boxing world champion Billy Joe Saunders has avoided immediate jail time after being involved in a violent brawl at a baby shower in Warwick. The 37-year-old was one of several men involved in the incident at Poppy’s Club in Bulkington on November 27, 2021.Saunders used a bottle to assault people during the fight, which later became a serious court case. Warwick Crown Court heard that one man was stabbed through the hand with a flick knife. Another person was allegedly seen carrying a gun. Saunders has now been handed a suspended prison sentence along with a fine and unpaid work.Billy Joe Saunders receives suspended sentence after violent brawlSaunders was sentenced to 15 months in prison, suspended for 18 months. He was also ordered to pay £1,000 ($1.3K) in costs and a £1,000 fine. He must complete 200 hours of unpaid work within the next 12 months.The court heard that nine men were involved in what was described as a “very violent” fight.The incident began earlier in the evening when two members of the group became involved in an argument. The situation then escalated again after midnight.Saunders did not initially join the fight. However, the judge said the former boxer became considerably involved after entering the brawl later.The judge said, “You were a boxer of some skill and repute at the Olympics and as a professional. You were involved in this (brawl) at a more serious level than three of those with you today (in the dock), as you used a bottle and were considerably involved in this offence, but I bear in mind you did not dive in at the outset, you got involved a little later.”A witness told the court that Saunders was “drunk, drinking a lot” during the event. The witness also claimed that the former fighter had been “derogatory” towards Irish people.Saunders’ lawyer, Sebastian Gardiner, told the court that his client’s life had spiralled after his defeat by Canelo Alvarez in May 2021.Gardiner said Saunders’ “world was tumbling down” at the time. He also said it was “an incident that took place at a time where he was extremely low, he had been drinking for the first time in his adult life.”The judge also said that Saunders’ experience as a professional boxer meant he “should be able to manage his feelings in a way others can’t”.The latest case adds to a difficult period away from boxing for the former champion. In 2024, Saunders was arrested over hare-coursing offences and was filmed directing a foul-mouthed rant at police. He later pleaded guilty to trespassing with dogs and being equipped for searching for or pursuing hares with dogs.In 2020, Saunders was fined £150K ($200K) over a video that appeared to condone domestic violence. Two years earlier, the British Boxing Board of Control fined him £100,000 ($132K) over another controversial video involving drugs and a sex act.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
