articles.title: Mauricio Pochettino: No 'Sporting Justice' For Tottenham In Man City Verdict
articles.summary: Ex-Tottenham manager Mauricio Pochettino expressed sadness at the lack of "sporting justice" that the reported verdict against Manchester City could bring.
articles.body: United States coach Mauricio Pochettino expressed sadness at an apparent failure of "sporting justice" in his response to reports that Manchester City has been found guilty of almost all of the 115 charges leveled against the club for alleged financial breaches. The alleged rule-breaking by City took place between 2009-18, during which period Pochettino was manager of Tottenham and turned the London team into a challenger for titles in English soccer despite operating on a relatively small budget. The Premier League has yet to officially confirm the verdict that, according to several media outlets, has been passed down by an independent commission following a long-running case. "If it’s true that the 114 rules were broken, then we lived through a period of deception," said Pochettino, speaking Monday — a day before the U.S. men’s team plays Chile in a friendly match. "So, whatever the punishment ends up being … I don’t know. It’s impossible to go back. I think a lot of damage has been done." Earlier this month, Pochettino called for Chelsea to be stripped of the 2016-17 Premier League title for a total of 74 breaches of Football Association regulations covering agents, working with intermediaries and third-party investment in players. Chelsea’s punishment, on appeal, was a fine of 10 million pounds ($13.4 million) and a suspended two-window transfer ban. Chelsea won the 2016-17 Premier League by a seven-point margin over Tottenham, which finished third in the 2017-18 season when City was champion. During this time, Tottenham was working under a far tighter budget than its title rivals in England yet still reached the Champions League final in 2019. Pochettino, who was at Spurs from 2014-19, said that "ultimately a lot of clubs followed the rules and others didn’t." "What’s going to happen — a financial penalty? Points deductions? I don’t know," he said. "It’s very difficult, honestly. Soccer Related StoriesProdigy. Next Big Thing. USA's Cavan Sullivan Is Just Focused On Playing.USMNT Star Chris Richards On Alabama, SEC Fans And The Magic Of WembleyWomen's World Cup Forces NWSL To Start Season Earlier In 2027 "It’s sad. It’s deeply sad. Because, in the end, we’ve entered into a situation where what was celebrated wasn’t really what we thought it was. What seemed so good maybe wasn’t so good. And what didn’t seem good maybe actually was good, but it couldn’t be seen as good because the other ‘good’ was achieved by breaking the rules. So, ultimately, we’ve lived through a period where sporting justice didn’t exist." City has always denied wrongdoing and its chairman, Khaldoon Al Mubarak, continued to protest the club's innocence on Saturday, a day after reports said a verdict had been reached. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Nike pone sus ojos en el pádel femenino: Delfi Brea, Martina Calvo y Andrea Ustero, las mejor colocadas
articles.standfirst: La firma estadounidense baraja ya varios nombres para su primer fichaje femenino que se uniría al publicado interés por Agustín Tapia en MARCA Pádel.
articles.summary: La firma estadounidense baraja ya varios nombres para su primer fichaje femenino que se uniría al publicado interés por Agustín Tapia en MARCA Pádel.
articles.body: Nike redobla su apuesta por el pádel. Si hace apenas unos meses MARCA adelantaba el interés por Agustín Tapia como primer embajador de la llegada al pádel de la multinacional norteamericana, ahora este periódico ha podido confirmar que ya hay varios nombres de jugadoras encima de la mesa siendo las mejor posicionadas Delfi Brea, Martina Calvo y Andrea Ustero. Desde hace varias semanas existen conversaciones abiertas para conocer la realidad de algunas de las mejores jugadoras del pádel actual y la firma estadounidense ya ha mantenido diversos contactos con el entorno de algunas de las estrellas para conocer su situación contractual y valorar así las diferentes posibilidades. Un interés creciente que según ha podido conocer este periódico se ha materializado en el pasado París Major cuando, como en Buenos Aires y Roma, un emisario de Nike estuvo presente durante el torneo y se produjeron diferentes conversaciones informales para confirmar que “existe interés” por varias jugadoras. Un fichaje que, a diferencia del ya publicado el pasado 15 de junio sobre el más que posible idilio entre Nike y Agustín Tapia para 2027, no estaría en una fase tan avanzada y viviría sus primeras conversaciones pudiendo producirse, según el perfil, la próxima temporada o llegado el 2028. El interés de Nike por el pádel femenino podría escenificarse con la misma estrategia que en el masculino apostando por su primera jugadora franquicia también con una número uno. Y, además, también con nacionalidad argentina. Y Delfi Brea sería el gran nombre. Movimientos que tendrían su origen en la grata impresión que se llevaron los emisarios americanos del torneo de Buenos Aires y el "fenómeno fan" que se genera allí y donde por primera vez el nombre de Brea habría empezado a valorarse como posible incorporación. La realidad es que 'La Elegida' tiene contrato en vigor con Bullpadel, la marca más consolidada del sector y con la que le une una larga y exitosa trayectoria desde que fuera una promesa, y Brea no contemplaría un movimiento en el que su actual marca no estuviera involucrada al considerarla “su casa”. Un interés que “está bien encaminado” según ha podido saber MARCA, pero que es dependiente de diversos acuerdos y patrocinios con vigencia contractual que han potenciado la carrera de la argentina desde que se convirtiera en atleta de la prestigiosa agencia estadounidense WME Sports que abrió su filial de pádel en 2024 y que también cuenta con Arturo Coello como cabeza de cartel. El nombre que con más fuerza suena en el pádel femenino esta temporada no ha pasado desapercibido también a ojos de los embajadores de Nike y Martina Calvo ya orbita en torno al interés de la multinacional deportiva habiéndose producido ya los primeros contactos. Con un ascenso meteórico en apenas año y medio en la élite profesional, ‘El Huracán’ ya es una de las jugadoras que más mueve dentro y fuera del circuito y su juventud, madurez y personalidad “son cualidades muy americanas”, comentan voces cercanas a los contactos, en clara alusión a la construcción de carreras y narrativas deportivas en USA. Babolat es el actual sponsor de Calvo en pala, calzado y bolsería, habiendo fichado en 2025 por Oysho, firma del Grupo Inditex, que viste a la joven jugadora dentro y fuera de pista y que está representada por la agencia española All In Sports Group y en la que también figuran nombres como Álvaro Morata o Raúl Asencio, Jessica Bouzas, Ángel Ayora o Coki Nieto. Para Martina y su entorno, la marca francesa es como su casa y prefieren optar por la cautela y el respeto a la misma en esta situación. “Apuntan también a Ustero”, ha sido la última información conocida por este periódcio para sumar el último nombre al interés de Nike por una jugadora de pádel y que señala al de la jugadora más joven que mejor está situada en el ranking y sobre el que muchas voces apuntan ya a próxima número uno. La catalana que ya despuntó prematuramente temporadas atrás convirtiéndose en aspirante al trono femenino con apenas 18 años, es uno de los grandes atractivos del pádel moderno por su facilidad para el deporte de la pala que quedó evidenciada, una vez más, en la final del Paris Major hace apenas unos días y que habría sorprendido positivamente a los embajadores de Nike presentes. La ‘Rebelde con causa’ es jugadora de Head desde la temporada 2023 cuando se convirtió en una de las apuestas de futuro de la firma austriaca y desde 2025 está representada por la agencia española Top Spin Agency, creada en 2023, y que unió a Ustero a otras estrellas del pádel como Sofía Araújo o Jon Sanz. Los primeros pasos de un nuevo movimiento de Nike en su llegada al pádel y que evidencian el claro crecimiento del pádel en el panorama internacional. El impulso definitivo para acabar de convertir en estrellas del deporte a las figuras más destacadas del circuito en la que para muchos es ya la redimensión del pádel profesional en la era Premier Padel y que se sumará a otros acuerdos ya conocidos con marcas multinacionales como Audemars Piguet, Qatar Airways, Red Bull o Heineken y las pioneras apuestas de ON, Rolex, Armani, Hublot, Skechers o Lacoste.

articles.title: Luke Littler: Luke Woodhouse calls for fans to 'appreciatate one-of-a-kind' darts sensation amid crowd booing
articles.summary: Luke Littler suffered a shock exit in the first round of the World Grand Prix on Monday night after he was beaten 2-1 by Luke Woodhouse; watch day two of the World Grand Prix live on Sky Sports+ from 6pm, Tuesday
articles.body:
Littler set out to defend his World Grand Prix title on Monday in Leicester, but was knocked out by Woodhouse in the first round , suffering a 2-1 defeat.

The world No 1 was seemingly not at his best during the match, averaging 82.41, with Woodhouse coming back from a set down to book a last-16 tie against Nathan Aspinall.

Reflecting on his victory, Woodhouse urged fans to get behind Littler, hailing him for how he has elevated the sport.

"Luke's not a robot. He is going to have days and weeks where he's not right on it," Woodhouse said.

"People have echoed it and I'm going to say it again: He's a one-of-a-kind, Luke Littler.

"I hope people will take the time to appreciate how good he is and not give him a hard time and I mean really sit behind him.

"You might not see another Luke Littler ever again."

Earlier in September, Littler was subjected to boos and whistles by some areas of the crowd during the World Series of Darts Finals in the Netherlands.

Littler was booed by fans during his opening match against Danny Noppert, before again being jeered during his round-of-16 match against Aspinall. In that match, referee Charlie Corstorphine was forced to intervene to settle the crowd.

The 19-year-old had also threatened to boycott events in the Netherlands, before later pulling out of two Players Championship events in the country. He was ultimately knocked out of the tournament in the quarter-finals by Jonny Clayton.

Asked why he thinks some have been giving the back-to-back PDC World Darts Championship winner a hard time, Woodhouse said: "I don't know.

"He's done for the game what Phil [Taylor], Michael van Gerwen, Raymond van Barneveld and Gary Anderson have done and has taken it to the next level.

"I just hope people get behind him, give him the support and appreciate what a top talent he is.

"OK, he wasn't on it tonight and last week he lost. But he's going to win so much more stuff."

On Monday night, Woodhouse bounced back from losing the first set to level the match, before getting off to a flying start in the third set.

He took the first two legs, before Littler hit back in the third. From there, Woodhouse would claim the final leg to win the deciding set 3-1, and wrapped up the match with a checkout of 75.

"It's very difficult to sum up; a mix of emotions," Woodhouse said on the victory.

"I thought I threw it away in the first set, well not threw away, but I had chances to take the first set to a deciding leg and when I didn't, I was so angry with myself.

"I felt he [Littler] wasn't flying on all gears, so, I thought: 'Please don't go out and lose two sets when he's not playing well. So, it's a relief.

"I'm over the moon to beat someone like Luke on a main stage."

Woodhouse added that sealing victory over the world No 1 was a huge achievement, but he added he was still hungry to win titles.

"Luke is going to go down as one of the greats, if not already.

"I'm not naive to the fact that it's a very short format; you've got to get out of the blocks quickly, double in, double out too, so I'm not naive to that.

"It's up there, but winning tournaments is what I'm here for."

The second round takes place across Wednesday and Thursday, with the quarter-finals on Friday, semi-finals on Saturday and final on Sunday.

articles.title: Pooja Singh bags Asian Games bronze in women’s high jump, ends India's 24-year wait
articles.summary: India’s Pooja Singh won the bronze medal in the women’s high jump at the 2026 Asian Games on Tuesday, clearing 1.84m in the final.
articles.body: India’s Pooja Singh won the bronze medal in the women’s high jump at the 2026 Asian Games on Tuesday, clearing 1.84m in the final. The 19-year-old’s best effort was below her personal best, but it was enough to earn her third place in Nagoya.Uzbekistan’s Sayfullaeva won gold with a personal best of 1.90m, while Kazakhstan’s Kristina Ovchinnikova took silver after clearing 1.87m.Pooja briefly moved into the lead after clearing 1.84m. However, she failed to clear 1.87m in all three attempts and had to settle for bronze.The medal caps a breakthrough season for Pooja, who is India’s national record-holder. She had earlier surpassed Sahana Kumari’s 14-year-old national record with a 1.93m clearance at the Asian Under-20 Athletics Championships.Pooja’s bronze was India’s first women’s high jump medal at the Asian Games since Bobby Aloysius won silver in 2002.Her podium finish came a day after Sarvesh Kushare won silver in the men’s high jump. Kushare cleared 2.25m, matching the winning height of Chinese Taipei’s Chao Hsuan-Fu. However, Chao took gold after clearing 2.25m in his first attempt, while Kushare needed two attempts at the height.Republic of Korea’s Sanghyeok Woo won bronze with a best clearance of 2.22m.Pooja’s bronze, along with Kushare’s silver and Parul Chaudhary’s bronze, added to India’s athletics medal haul at the Asian Games.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Parveen Hooda’s redemption hour: From a lost medal to a shot at Asian Games boxing gold
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: As Parveen Hooda unleashes fury inside the ring, she is fighting battles far beyond it.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: As Parveen Hooda unleashes fury inside the ring, she is fighting battles far beyond it. The Rohtak boxer is punching at more than an opponent now. Every counter carries the weight of a medal taken away, an Olympic dream that vanished, and a family waiting for relief. The road here has been paved with setbacks, sacrifice and a hunger for redemption.Three years ago, Parveen won bronze at the Hangzhou Games. Then came the whereabouts failure, a 22-month suspension and the stripping of her medal. Paris Olympics slipped away. Her Glasgow CWG return in July-Aug ended in a quarterfinal defeat. Now, in Aichi-Nagoya, she has fought her way back to the Asian Games final, beating China’s Li Shu 5-0 in the 65kg semifinal.A silver is assured. But Parveen is not looking back. She wants gold — and full redemption.Her fight has always extended beyond the ring. Her father, Lakhpat Hooda, has been battling cancer for four years and is also a heart patient. Her mother, Neelam Devi, sells buffalo milk to keep the household running, while Parveen’s 20-year-old younger brother is studying. An ITBP assistant sub-inspector, Parveen has become the family’s principal breadwinner, using her boxing earnings and salary for her father’s treatment.“Her father would be super proud of her achievement, as is her mother. Parveen takes care of every need of the family,” her childhood coach Sudhir Hooda told TOI. “She has been funding her father’s medical treatment with cash awards from boxing and her ITBP income.”Hooda first saw Parveen in April 2010. She was in class five, barely 22kg, and came from a family that struggled to afford boxing nutrition. "I became the village sarpanch and opened an academy in Rohtak to keep youngsters away from drugs and crime, offering 80 children free coaching, milk and diet. Parveen was one of the brightest."Parveen’s rise was swift as she won state and national sub-junior gold in 2012. After a long period when competitions were disrupted (Indian Boxing Federation was suspended from 2012-2016), she broke into the youth ranks in 2017 and entered the national camp in 2018. South Asian Games gold followed in 2019, then Asian Championships gold and Worlds bronze in 2022.Against Li in Nishio, she stayed composed, picking her counters and controlling distance. She now faces Chinese Taipei’s Paris Olympic bronze medallist Chen Nien-chin for gold. “I hope for the gold, and I will give my best to take it,” she said afterwards. Parveen is only the third Indian woman to reach an Asian Games final, after Mary Kom (gold 2014) and Lovlina Borgohain (silver 2023).Ankush Panghal provided another headline, stunning reigning 75kg world champion Fazliddin Erkinboev of Uzbekistan 4-1 in the 80kg semifinal. After dropping the opening round, Ankush changed gears, attacked the body and dominated the finish. He is India’s first male Asian Games finalist since Amit Panghal in 2018.Narender Berwal secured bronze after a 0-5 loss to reigning world champion Aibek Oralbay of Kazakhstan in the +90kg semifinal. It is his second straight Asian Games bronze.With Parveen and Ankush chasing gold, India has six medals assured from 11 entries. Three more semifinal bouts — Priya Ghanghas, Kapil Pokhariya and Lovlina Borgohain — await on Wednesday, raising hopes of an even bigger Indian medal haul.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asian Games 2026 Day 10: Neeru Dhanda, women’s 4x400m relay shine as 8-medal haul takes India past 50
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Neeru Dhanda delivered India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the women’s trap event despite heavy rain and chilly conditions, before the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Neeru Dhanda delivered India’s first-ever Asian Games gold in the women’s trap event despite heavy rain and chilly conditions, before the women’s 4x400m relay team added another gold in the evening to make Tuesday a fruitful Day 10 for India at the Aichi-Nagoya Games.The golden double helped India breach the 50-medal mark and climb back into the top 10 of the overall medal standings. India ended the day with 53 medals — six gold, 21 silver and 26 bronze — to sit 10th in the table.The two gold medals also ended India’s wait for a top podium finish after two days without a gold, following the double triumph in kabaddi on September 26.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleNeeru braves rain to make historyDhanda produced one of the standout performances of the Games as she battled incessant rain and difficult visibility to win the women’s trap individual gold.The Indian shooter remained composed despite the conditions and finished with 28 hits in the final, setting an Asian Games record in the process.It was a landmark result for Indian shooting as Dhanda became the country’s first-ever women’s trap champion at the Asian Games. Her victory was also India’s first individual shooting gold of the ongoing edition.Dhanda’s success came on a day when the weather repeatedly tested athletes across disciplines, but she managed to maintain her concentration when it mattered most.India added another shooting medal on the day, with Dhanda, Aashima Ahlawat and Manisha Keer taking silver in the women’s trap team event.Women’s relay delivers second goldIndia’s second gold came in the evening through the women’s 4x400m relay team of Kiran, Prachi Choudhary, MR Poovamma and Vithya Ramraj.The quartet clocked 3:29.69 to finish on top and provide India with its first athletics gold of the Games.For Poovamma, the victory added another chapter to an impressive Asian Games career. The 36-year-old had also been part of India’s gold-medal winning 4x400m relay teams at the 2014 and 2018 editions.Vithya, meanwhile, capped a memorable Games campaign with another medal after earlier bettering PT Usha’s more than four-decade-old national record in the women’s 400m hurdles.The relay gold provided a much-needed high point for India’s athletics campaign, which has otherwise produced a mixed set of results in Aichi-Nagoya.Gulveer completes medal trebleNineteen-year-old high jumper Pooja Singh added a bronze after clearing 1.84m, while Gulveer Singh continued his remarkable run by winning bronze in the men’s 5000m.Gulveer had already won silver in the 10,000m and 1500m and thus completed a treble of track and field medals at these Games.His achievement put him in elite company. Gulveer became only the second Indian man to win three track and field medals at a single Asian Games after Lavy Pinto, who won gold in the 100m and 200m and silver in the 4x100m relay at the inaugural 1951 edition.India also secured bronze in the mixed 4x100m relay, with Gurindervir Singh, Sneha Sathyanarayana, Animesh Kujur and Harita Bhadra clocking a season-best 41.06 seconds.The men’s 4x400m relay quartet of Vishal TK, Dharamveer Choudhary, Jay Kumar and T Manu also finished with bronze in 3:01.61. India could not defend the gold won at the previous edition.The country, however, drew a blank in both the men’s and women’s 800m finals.The athletics medal haul remained well short of India’s six golds from the previous edition, but the women’s relay triumph ensured the campaign ended Day 10 on a high.Boxing continues to deliverIndia’s boxing campaign also received a major boost as Ankush Panghal reached the men’s 80kg final, ending an eight-year wait for an Indian male boxing finalist at the Asian Games.Ankush produced a stirring comeback to defeat reigning 75kg world champion Fazliddin Erkinboev of Uzbekistan 4-1 and book his place in the gold-medal bout.Parveen Hooda also advanced to the final of the women’s 65kg category after a commanding 5-0 victory over China’s Li Shu.Narender Berwal, meanwhile, signed off with a bronze after losing 0-5 to reigning super-heavyweight world champion Aibek Oralbay of Kazakhstan in the +90kg semifinal.The medal was Narender’s second Asian Games bronze after he also finished on the podium at Hangzhou in 2023.India’s boxers have now ensured six medals at these Games, surpassing their previous haul of four.Volleyball team stages stunning comebackThe Indian men’s volleyball team also advanced to the quarterfinals after producing a remarkable comeback against Qatar.India recovered from two sets down to defeat Qatar 26-28, 25-27, 25-23, 25-20, 24-22 in a marathon Pool C encounter that lasted two hours and 47 minutes.The victory completed a perfect group-stage run for India, which had earlier defeated Vietnam 3-0 and Hong Kong China 3-0.All four quarterfinals will be played on Thursday.Archers make progressIndia also made progress in the recurve events, with Dhiraj Bommadevara, Neeraj Chauhan and Kumkum Mohod Anil advancing to the quarterfinals.Chauhan produced one of the biggest results of the day when he stunned South Korea’s Kim Je Deok, a three-time Olympic gold-medallist, 6-4 in the men’s individual 1/8 elimination round.Bommadevara also advanced after defeating Chinese Taipei’s Cheng Hsiang-Hui 6-2.In the women’s recurve event, Kumkum Mohod Anil defeated Bangladesh’s Saima Salah Uddin 6-0 to reach the last eight.Squash, tennis add winsThe Indian women’s squash team completed a 3-0 win over Iran in its final group-stage match to advance to the quarterfinals.Tanvi Khanna was declared the winner after Iran’s Narges Soltani retired while trailing. Anahat Singh then defeated Fereshteh Eghtedari 3-0 before veteran Joshna Chinappa completed the clean sweep with a 3-0 win over Najmeh Boushehrizadeh.India will face Singapore in the quarterfinals on Wednesday.In tennis, Dhakshineswar Suresh and Sumit Nagal made winning starts to their men’s singles campaigns and secured places in the pre-quarterfinals.Dhakshineswar defeated Indonesia’s Gunawan Trismuwantara 7-5, 7-6(2), while Nagal overcame South Korea’s Seongchan Hong 6-4, 6-0 in a rain-interrupted contest.Cycling, however, provided disappointment, with India’s riders failing to advance from the preliminary stages in the men’s and women’s team sprint and women’s team pursuit events.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Teresa Perales, homenajeada en la recepción al equipo español de natación paralímpica
articles.standfirst: José Manuel Rodríguez Uribes recibió en el CSD a una representación de la selección que compitió en los Europeos de Kocaeli (Turquía)
articles.summary: José Manuel Rodríguez Uribes recibió en el CSD a una representación de la selección que compitió en los Europeos de Kocaeli (Turquía)
articles.body: El presidente del Consejo Superior de Deportes (CSD), José Manuel Rodríguez Uribes, recibió a una representación de la selección española de natación paralímpica que conquistó 46 metales en los Europeos de Kocaeli (Turquía). Durante el acto se homenajeó a Teresa Perales por llegar a las cien medallas internacionales. La delegación española en Kocaeli estuvo integrada por 44 nadadores pertenecientes a las federaciones españolas de Deportes de Personas con Discapacidad Física (FEDDF), de Deportes para Ciegos (FEDC) y de Personas con Parálisis Cerebral y Daño Cerebral Adquirido (FEDPC) sumando entre todos 46 medallas repartidas en nueve oros, diecisiete platas y veinte bronces en la cita continental. "Vuestros éxitos deportivos no son casualidad. Tienen que ver con vuestro talento, con el trabajo de las federaciones y con el acompañamiento e impulso del Comité Paralímpico Español", dijo en la sede del CSD Rodríguez Uribes, que reconoció "el esfuerzo" de los nadadores para lograr estos éxitos. El momento más simbólico de la recepción fue el homenaje a Teresa Perales por haber alcanzado las 100 medallas internacionales durante el reciente Campeonato de Europa. La nadadora aragonesa cerró su participación en Turquía con cinco podios (un oro, tres platas y un bronce) que redondean un palmarés excelso. No en vano, su centenar de preseas se distribuye entre 28 medallas en Juegos Paralímpicos, 23 en campeonatos del Mundo y 49 en Campeonatos de Europa. "Me siento una privilegiada, como muchos de los deportistas que estamos aquí, por tener la oportunidad de entrenar en el Centro de Alto Rendimiento de Madrid, de vivir en la residencia deportiva y de convivir con deportistas de otras disciplinas, con o sin discapacidad, que deseamos conseguir lo mejor para nuestro país", dijo la nadadora aragonesa. Más allá del hito de Teresa Perales, el Campeonato de Europa de Kocaeli volvió a poner de manifiesto el extraordinario nivel de la natación paralímpica española, sobresaliendo las actuaciones de Tasy Dmytriv y Nahia Zudaire con seis medallas. La delegación española mejoró el resultado obtenido en la anterior edición del Campeonato de Europa, disputada en Madeira (Portugal) en 2024, cuando España conquistó 39 medallas. "España ha sido la cuarta mejor selección europea, lo que indica que estamos en una posición privilegiada. Por supuesto, sobresale la figura de Teresa Perales y sus 100 medallas internacionales, pero también se están consolidando nadadores jóvenes que llegan desde la base. Eso no solo significa que nuestro país cuenta con grandes figuras, sino que existe relevo", declaró Enrique Álvarez, presidente de la FEDDF. En la misma línea, Francisco Botía destacó el trabajo que el Comité Paralímpico Español realiza en colaboración con el Consejo Superior de Deportes, las federaciones deportivas españolas y los patrocinadores privados para detectar talento y acompañar a los deportistas en su camino a la élite. "Es una fórmula que en la natación funciona, con la Liga AXA, y que vamos a seguir explorando", apuntó

articles.title: Fantasy Football Waiver Wire, Week 4: Braelon Allen, Ollie Gordon II among top pickups to target
articles.summary: Justin Boone takes you through his Week 4 fantasy football waiver wire column with top pickups, injuries to note and streamers.
articles.body:
Every Monday during the season, Justin Boone breaks down the recommended waiver-wire pickups.

Roster percentages are generated from Yahoo leagues. Free-Agent Budget (FAB) amounts are based on a $100 salary cap. Only players rostered in less than 50% of leagues are considered.

Darnold returned from injury with a massive 379-yard, four-touchdown effort against the Commanders.

It was far from a flawless performance, since he did throw two interceptions and the Seahawks ultimately lost the game. However, Darnold reminded everyone that he can be a viable fantasy streaming option. Don't forget, last year Darnold put up seven top-10 weekly finishes.

While I wouldn't want to roll with him as my fantasy starter, he's someone you can use to cover injuries or bye weeks.

Desperation streaming options (if starter is out)

Injuries hit the NFL hard for a second straight week and several backfields have been altered by them. Though De'Von Achane is reportedly out for the season with a torn ACL, the Dolphins offense doesn't offer the same high-end potential that exists in New York.

It's unknown how much time (if any) Breece Hall will miss after suffering a quad injury on Sunday, but he at least has a strong backup waiting in the wings. After the game, Hall said he felt "something" before getting tackled and then felt more pain when he was tackled. Aaron Glenn is notorious for his limited information on injuries, so we might not get an update here until later in the week.

In the meantime, I'm trying to add Allen everywhere I don't already have him stashed. Prior to Hall getting hurt, Allen had already shown he can provide weekly flex value as the No. 2 option for the Jets, totaling 40 scrimmage yards on 10 touches in Week 1 and then finding the end zone in Week 2.

The Jets upcoming schedule is also favorable with the Bears, Browns and Dolphins in three of their next four contests. Allen will have top-24 fantasy RB upside if Hall is sidelined. Managers in deep leagues can also consider stashing Isaiah Davis , who would slot in as the complementary piece in the event of a Hall absence.

Achane tearing his ACL in Week 3 is an awful outcome for one of the most talented backs in the league. With Achane out for the year, Miami will be looking for a new starter and fantasy managers are hungry for usable RB options.

Unfortunately, I'm taking a slightly more cautious approach on this backfield. Gordon was the next man up on Sunday, but his path had been cleared with Wright ruled out due to multiple injuries (stinger, foot). If Wright was healthy, we don't know exactly how the Dolphins would have distributed touches.

Until we see Wright back at practice, Gordon is in line to start. However, he only managed an extremely inefficient 55 yards on 20 touches against the Chiefs — saving his fantasy day with a touchdown. A date with the Vikings in Week 4 isn't exactly a matchup to target, since Brian Flores' defense will be a nightmare for Malik Willis and company. Minnesota has also held every back they've faced under 50 rushing yards and has yet to allow a TD to an RB.

Feel free to add Gordon if you need running back help, I'm just worried we could see that inefficiency continue and an eventual split with Wright seems likely. Consider Gordon a TD-or-bust RB3 for now, while Wright is a sneaky add who could emerge as the starter once healthy.

Travis Etienne Jr. battled a hamstring issue during practice last week, before turning in a full practice on Friday and being removed from the injury report. Unfortunately, he suffered an aggravation in the game and is now at risk of missing time.

To make matters worse, the Saints don't have a great second option who can scoop up all the volume. Kellen Moore also hasn't shown a willingness to give one back a major workload this season, instead opting to deploy a committee approach.

The 31-year-old Kamara has been a declining player for a couple seasons, so it wasn't surprising to see him only compile an embarrassing 22 yards on 14 touches in Week 2. The results were slightly better on Sunday, with 41 yards on 10 attempts.

It's still hard to imagine Kamara finding the fountain of youth and becoming anything more than a risky RB3. That's why I've also highlighted Miller here, who could carve out a bigger role next to the struggling veteran. Bottom line, even with Etienne at risk of missing time, if you're investing in the Saints backfield you should expect more than RB3 fantasy value.

Woody Marks is 52% rostered but would be the No. 4 RB add behind Allen, Gordon and Kamara, if available.

Zach Charbonnet is 51% rostered but can be added as an IR stash, if available.

Best one-injury away backup RBs to stash

Chris Rodriguez Jr. at CIN (40% rostered)

Dart-throw flex options (if starter is out)

With Alec Pierce on injured reserve indefinitely, the Colts' passing attack is consolidating around Josh Downs , Tyler Warren and Allen.

All three came away with strong stat lines on Sunday, but the fact a 34-year-old Allen earned nine targets and produced six catches for 63 yards and a touchdown against a tough Texans defense is impressive.

Allen gets a much softer opponent in Week 4, when the Colts head to Washington to face the Commanders defense that ranks inside the top-10 for fantasy points allowed to receivers through three weeks.

While I wouldn't overspend on an older wideout like Allen, he's firmly in the conversation as a fantasy WR3/flex moving forward.

With Caleb Douglas sitting out due to an ankle injury, the Dolphins' receiving corps shifted more in favor of Bell and Washington.

Bell had the best day of his young career, playing 71% of the time and catching four balls for 67 yards on seven targets. That's a strong outing for a talented rookie who is well ahead of schedule in his return from a torn ACL last year.

Meanwhile, Washington has been a solid WR4/flex option for three consecutive weeks, topping 50 scrimmage yards in every game so far.

As I mentioned with their backfield, investing in the Dolphins offense might not feel that enticing, but there is certainly opportunity and value here.

Washington is a low-ceiling, high-floor starter, with Bell being the more intriguing pickup for his untapped ceiling. Even Douglas is worth stashing to see if he returns to practice this week.

Denzel Boston is 48% rostered but would be the No. 1 WR add, if available.

Makai Lemon is 50% rostered but would be the No. 2 WR add behind Boston, if available.

Dontayvion Wicks is 50% rostered but would be the No. 3 WR add behind Boston and Lemon, if available.

Jordyn Tyson is 52% rostered but can be added as an IR stash, if available.

Sadiq has been highlighted every week in this space, after a preseason injury caused the first-rounder to get off to a slow start. Even so, he still found the end zone on a manufactured touch in Week 1 and his role was always going to grow as he got more comfortable in the offense.

The injury to fellow tight end Mason Taylor made Sadiq a top-10 pickup in this column last week. When wideout Adonai Mitchell hurt his finger in practice, it pushed Sadiq into must-add territory, especially given the matchup with a Lions defense that had given up the most points to fantasy tight ends in the first two games. That's why I highlighted him on Fantasy Football Live Sunday morning.

The result was seven receptions, 105 yards and a touchdown — and we're only scratching the surface on this potential TE1 rest of season.

Ferguson is now expected to miss Week 4, but he's still an add given his upside with the uncertainty around Puka Nacua's injury.

Coming off a 6-54-1 stat line in Week 2, Ferguson was poised for another monster outing as Puka Nacua continues to recover from a hip/groin injury. Sadly, an ankle injury destroyed the chances of a repeat performance and led to Ferguson only playing 26% of the snaps on Sunday night.

It hurt even more to watch Tyler Higbee erupt for eight grabs, 62 yards and a score with Ferguson watching from the sidelines.

At any point in the season, if Nacua or Davante Adams are out and Ferguson is healthy, the second-year tight end will be a strong TE1 play — so don't give up on him yet.

Favorable upcoming schedules: Bengals (42% rostered), Raiders (7% rostered), Commanders (1% rostered)

Will Reichard is 58% rostered mark but would be the No. 1 K add, if available.

Quarterbacks: Justin Herbert , Baker Mayfield, Malik Willis

Tight Ends: Kyle Pitts Sr., Hunter Henry

The list of drop candidates grows as the weeks pass. Injuries are responsible for some of these names making the list, like Mayfield, Brooks, Spears and Reed.

Herbert has struggled through three games and his upcoming schedule is horrific with the Seahawks, Broncos, Chiefs before a Week 7 bye, then the Rams, Texans and Ravens immediately after it.

We've seen enough from Lloyd to know he's not going to be the answer behind the Packers' struggling offensive line.

Godwin, Thomas, Harrison, Johnston, Worthy and Shakir and risky flex plays who haven't done much through three weeks.

articles.title: Bolillo Gómez encaró a periodismo salvadoreño tras dolorosa goleada y piden su cabeza
articles.standfirst: Tras la dura derrota con la Selección de El Salvador, Hernán Darío ‘Bolillo’ Gómez tuvo un tenso cruce con los medios de comunicación
articles.summary: Tras la dura derrota con la Selección de El Salvador, Hernán Darío ‘Bolillo’ Gómez tuvo un tenso cruce con los medios de comunicación
articles.body: La tensión en la Selección de El Salvador llegó a su punto de ebullición. Tras encajar una aparatosa y humillante derrota por 6-0 ante Guatemala en condición de visitante —por la segunda fecha del Grupo B en la Liga de Naciones de la Concacaf—, el estratega colombiano Hernán Darío ‘Bolillo’ Gómez dio la cara ante la prensa centroamericana y dejó clara su postura respecto a su futuro en el banquillo. El experimentado técnico antioqueño de 70 años, quien asumió la dirección técnica de La Selecta a principios de 2025, no esquivó la responsabilidad tras la debacle en suelo guatemalteco y dejó su cargo a disposición de las directivas. Durante la rueda de prensa posterior al compromiso, el ‘Bolillo’ reconoció la magnitud del tropezón y utilizó su habitual franqueza para referirse al momento crítico que atraviesa el proceso deportivo. “El presidente tiene todo el derecho a tomar decisiones, las que él vea y se sienta dentro de lo que pasó hoy. ¿No acaban de echar al de Costa Rica? Pues que me echen a mí también. Con esto lo tienen que echar a uno”, aseveró el entrenador. El técnico colombiano hizo un paralelo con su trayectoria internacional para dimensionar la gravedad del marcador: “Por allá me pasó un 6-1, también con Ecuador, y lo primero que dije fue: 'este es un resultado que saca a los técnicos'. ¿Qué podemos hacer? Es más fácil echar a uno que a 22. Buenas noches”, sentenció antes de dar por terminada la comparecencia. Las declaraciones de Gómez llevan un mensaje teledirigido hacia Yamil Bukele, presidente de la Federación Salvadoreña de Fútbol y hermano del mandatario nacional Nayib Bukele. Con la presión mediática en su punto más alto, el dirigente de la FESFUT tiene en sus manos la decisión de ratificar o cesar al colombiano en las próximas horas. La afición salvadoreña ha reaccionado de manera contundente en plataformas digitales, exigiendo de forma masiva la salida inmediata del estratega. El ambiente en torno al equipo nacional viene deteriorado desde la no clasificación al Mundial 2026, objetivo primordial para el que fue contratado el entrenador. Los titulares de los principales medios de comunicación en El Salvador no guardaron contemplaciones ante el abultado marcador: En medio de una oleada de destituciones en la región de Concacaf —donde recientemente se confirmó la salida de estregas como Fernando Batista en Costa Rica—, la continuidad de Hernán Darío Gómez pende de un hilo y la FESFUT definirá en breve el rumbo del seleccionado centroamericano.

articles.standfirst: Galán reveló cuándo estará listo el nuevo Estadio El Campín en Bogotá
articles.summary: Galán reveló cuándo estará listo el nuevo Estadio El Campín en Bogotá
articles.body: El alcalde de Bogotá, Carlos Fernando Galán, confirmó que el proyecto para la construcción y renovación del nuevo estadio Nemesio Camacho El Campín sufrirá cambios en sus tiempos de ejecución. A pesar de que la fecha inicial fijada para la entrega era diciembre de 2027, los retrasos en los trámites previos han obligado a revisar la programación formal de las obras. Uno de los principales factores que ha impedido el inicio formal de las obras de construcción es la tramitación de permisos y estudios clave. Entre ellos destaca la aprobación del Estudio de Tránsito y Transporte por parte de la Secretaría Distrital de Movilidad, un insumo fundamental para regular el flujo vehicular y de peatones en la zona de influencia del escenario deportivo. Aunque en marzo de 2026 se llevó a cabo un acto simbólico de inicio, las etapas de construcción física continuaban detenidas a la espera de estos avales institucionales. "Muy pronto vamos a tener un anuncio... Nos tocó fue salvar este proyecto, que como le digo tenía un 'pecado original', que como estaba planteado no era viable. Ya le daremos la fecha y las características exactas; la ciudad va a respaldar este proyecto porque nos va a ilusionar con tener uno de los mejores estadios de Latinoamérica", señaló el mandatario local. El nuevo complejo deportivo y cultural se desarrolla mediante el modelo de Asociación Público-Privada (APP), con la participación del concesionario Sencia. La Alcaldía Mayor anunciará próximamente las fechas definitivas de entrega y los detalles técnicos finales del escenario deportivo.

articles.title: Ireland undecided on approach for next game against Israel, coach says
articles.summary: Ireland played the first Nations League game despite unease among some players over Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza.
articles.body:
Ireland have yet to decide how they will approach their second Nations League match against Israel on Sunday, coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said in comments reported by Irish media.

The remarks, reported on Tuesday, emerged two days after Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in Hungary following a turbulent build-up in which the squad voted to fulfil the fixture despite unease among some players over Israel’s genocidal war in Gaza.

“We haven’t decided what we will do 100 percent,” Hallgrimsson said when asked about the return fixture, according to Irish media.

“When we get home tonight, we’ll give them a day off tomorrow to go home, and share a day with their families and friends and loved ones, and then we’ll come back and prepare for the Austria game.

“Hopefully we can finish that one and take a discussion.”

Ireland face Austria on Thursday in Dublin before their designated home match against Israel, which will be played behind closed doors in Backa Topola, Serbia.

Hallgrimsson said that there were differing views within his squad.

“All I can say is I think we are all uncomfortable, number one,” he said.

“Number two, we have different opinions, and we should allow people to have different opinions. It’s not one opinion that’s right and all the others are wrong.”

The Icelandic coach made the comments following Sunday’s match in Debrecen, where Ireland’s players wore black armbands in recognition of all the lives lost in Gaza and bowed their heads as the Israeli national anthem was played at the near-empty stadium.

The teams skipped the traditional pre-match handshakes and did not exchange pennants.

Only one player, goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu, pulled out , saying “it would be wrong to participate” in either the match or the return fixture in Serbia on October 4 due to the “killing of innocent people”.

Hallgrimsson said that his players had nevertheless “raised awareness worldwide” through their actions.

Since Ireland were drawn in the same Nations League group as Israel in February, sportspeople, fan groups and pro-Palestinian campaigners have called for the fixtures to be boycotted.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) itself requested last year that UEFA suspend Israel but failed to secure sufficient support from European football chiefs.

The FAI moved Ireland’s October 4 match against Israel from Dublin to Serbia, citing “operational challenges”.

Israel strongly rejects allegations that its conduct in Gaza amounts to genocide, but an independent United Nations commission of inquiry has found that Israeli military actions and warfare methods in Gaza constitute genocide.

articles.title: Trail Blazers Affirm Commitment to Stay in Portland
articles.summary: Team president said they're aiming to finalize a lease extension and renovation deal.
articles.body:
Cooler heads could be prevailing in the Portland arena saga, as the Trail Blazers have publicly signaled their intent to stay at the Moda Center.

Speaking at the team's preseason media day, Blazers president Dewayne Hankins said the team is aiming to finalize a lease extension and renovation deal to remain at the 31-year-old, publicly owned arena.

"We are committed to a deal that works for our ownership. We are committed to a deal that works for our public partners," Hankins said. "We are doing everything we can to ensure the Trail Blazers are staying right here."

Those comments mark a notable change in tone compared to much of the year, during which the newly arrived team owner Tom Dundon took a hard line on the ongoing arena negotiations. In June, Dundon said taxpayers should shoulder the entire cost of the renovations , stoking fears of an imminent franchise relocation, and the team later called a working term sheet a "non-starter." Hankins then called the Portland business climate "stagnant," creating further division with public officials.

Since then, the state of Oregon, Multnomah County, and the city of Portland have approved a framework that would collectively provide $586 million for Moda Center upgrades . Still, there are hurdles to clear, including a city push for the Blazers to pay rent and income tax and hire union workers.

The state portion of that money, representing more than half of the entire package, also has a December deadline, creating a time crunch to finalize an agreement.

"These conversations continue to happen behind closed doors, and it's most productive for us when they stay that way," Hankins said. "What I will say is this: We are committed to Portland."

Earlier this month, NBA commissioner Adam Silver said he would consider it a "failure" if the arena deal collapses and the franchise leaves Portland.

Portland Mayor Keith Wilson recently urged the two sides to pick up the pace of negotiations, something Hankins said he was open to doing.

"The mayor the other week said he wanted us to meet every day. We'll make time to do that if we need to do that," Hankins said.

Blazers star Damian Lillard also struck a hopeful tone at the team's media day.

"I don't see a world where the Trail Blazers aren't in Portland. I just don't," he said. "And I do pray that day never comes, even when I'm done. I know how important the Trail Blazers are to this city."

articles.title: Tyson Fury manager provides update on start time for Anthony Joshua fight in Cardiff
articles.summary: Spencer Brown said the start time for the fight is still being negotiated
articles.body:
Tyson Fury 's manager has weighed in on the debate surrounding the upcoming fight between Fury and Anthony Joshua , arguing its start time should be brought forward for the benefit of a UK audience.

The heavyweight clash, slated for 11 December at Cardiff's Principality Stadium , is currently expected to start at 2am local time, more suitable to a primetime audience in the US.

Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn had previously said that was too late for an event taking place in the UK, with Fury's manager Spencer Brown now voicing his agreement and saying that the 2am start had not been formally confirmed.

He told Playbook Boxing : "I think 2am is far too late.

"I think that the general public in England will want to watch it in the pubs, the clubs, you know, around each other's houses.

"There'll be a party atmosphere. And I just think it needs to be earlier. Simple as that.

"It's all in negotiation at the moment but we think it shouldn't be at 2am. 99% of people would tell you that."

"People don't want to be in a stadium at 2am freezing. We're still negotiating it, it's ongoing."

The British heavyweights' duel will be shown live on Netflix , with ring walks potentially taking place in the early hours of the following morning to suit the American audience.

Fury pushed for an American venue for the clash but protests from Joshua and Hearn meant the UK was chosen as the destination.

The fight was plunged into doubt after Ring Magazine journalist Mike Coppinger suggested it could be called off due to unspecified "issues" over the weekend, although those have reportedly been ironed out , with a press conference set to go ahead in London on Wednesday.

articles.title: NHL rumors: 3 reasons Blue Jackets GM Don Waddell traded Kirill Marchenko
articles.summary: The National Hockey League got one last blockbuster trade just over 24 hours before the start of the 2026-27 season, with Kirill Marchenko and Matthew Knies...
articles.body:
The National Hockey League got one last blockbuster trade just over 24 hours before the start of the 2026-27 season, with Kirill Marchenko and Matthew Knies headlining a swap between the Columbus Blue Jackets and Toronto Maple Leafs .

It had become increasingly clear that Marchenko had no interest in re-signing in Ohio . That was not the case in Ontario: the Russian forward inked a six-year, $75 million extension that will keep him with the Leafs through 2032-33.

Sportsnet hockey insider Elliotte Friedman offered some insight into the trade Tuesday, pointing to three reasons Blue Jackets general manager Don Waddell decided to make the deal.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"Columbus GM Don Waddell made it clear he didn't have to trade an unhappy Marchenko yet, especially as the Blue Jackets hope to compete for a playoff berth. There were at least three reasons he reconsidered," Friedman wrote in his latest 32 Thoughts. "First, they were never offered anyone as appetizing as Knies, especially since he's locked in at great value. He will benefit from 'quiet,' not being in three trade rumours per week. Teammates believed he was annoyed at the speculation; had enough of it.

"Second, the Maple Leafs think so highly of Marchenko — an absolute superstud in their eyes — they were willing to take Elvis Merzlikins and Miles Wood to get it done. They tried their best to hide their interest, but lusted after him, feeling he has the highest ceiling of anyone in this trade.

"Third, the relationship between Marchenko and head coach Rick Bowness was … uneasy. One very interesting thing: Months ago, word was Marchenko would go to Montreal no problem, but he wasn't as certain about Toronto. Whatever his initial concerns, he warmed up when it really mattered."

Marchenko will immediately slot into Toronto's top six, and it wouldn't be surprising to see him play on Auston Matthews ' wing. Alternatively, he could line up alongside John Tavares on the second line. Either way, the Leafs' forward group is looking dangerous again ahead of the new season.

General manager John Chayka said he hopes Marchenko can make his Leafs debut against the Montreal Canadiens on Tuesday night, provided his immigration paperwork is completed. If he does suit up, he'll have a chance to play alongside the most accomplished forwards of his NHL career.

After posting 141 points over the last two seasons, Marchenko could push for a point-per-game campaign for the first time, and the 26-year-old is now firmly entrenched as a key piece of Toronto's core.

articles.title: William and Kate surprise Sinfield on MND run
articles.summary: The Royal couple greeted the former rugby legend as he finished up day three of his charity run.
articles.body:
The Prince and Princess of Wales surprised Sir Kevin Sinfield as he finished the third day of his latest endurance challenge to raise money for motor neurone disease (MND).

The Leeds Rhino legend is aiming to complete seven ultramarathons in seven days, inspired by his late friend Rob Burrow, who died in 2024 after living with the disease for four years.

As he arrived at the DIY Kitchens Stadium in Wakefield he was greeted by William and Kate, who stopped to chat to him and his team.

William previously "surprised" Sinfield when he turned up to Headingley Stadium in 2024 to present him and Burrow with their CBEs for services to fundraising.

Sinfield began day three of his challenge at Bishopthorpe Palace in York, before passing through places including Tadcaster and Castleford.

Along the route he was joined by England rugby union head coach Steve Borthwick, former Olympian Steve Cram and Charlie Ireland from Clarkson's Farm.

Sinfield is aiming to run between Hull and Manchester, visiting all 12 Super League clubs before arriving at the Grand Final on Saturday.

During the 7 in 7: The Grand Finale challenge, each ultra marathon is split into 7km blocks which must be completed within the hour before beginning the next.

There will also be an "extra mile" event each day, where Sir Kevin joins members of the MND community in completing four laps of a running track.

Earlier William and Kate visited Headingley stadium in Leeds, where they met Leeds Rhinos CEO Jamie Jones Buchanan MBE- a lifelong friend of Burrow - and former captain Danny McGuire.

They also met representatives from the Leeds Rhinos Foundation and spoke about how it uses "the power of sport" to help young people.

Listen to highlights from West Yorkshire on BBC Sounds , catch up with the latest episode of Look North .

articles.title: Brock Faber timeline unknown after skull fracture, surgery
articles.summary: The Minnesota Wild defenseman will miss the start of the regular season, and potentially much longer.
articles.body:
Brock Faber suffered a skull fracture when he was hit in the head by a puck last Friday night.

Faber underwent surgery on Sunday. There is no timetable for Faber's return.

"Brock Faber suffered a fracture to his skull. He had surgery on Sunday that was successful. We'll update you guys at some point in time on a possible return to play," Wild general manager Bill Guerin said. "Brock's at home. He's doing well. He's just resting, and we're going to leave it at that."

Could the injury keep him out for the entire season?

"I'm not getting into any of that right now," Guerin answered. "He just had a serious surgery. He's doing well. He's doing really well, which is good news. We'll follow the doctor's leads."

Faber was injured when Miro Heiskanen's shot hit him in the side of the head during the intense preseason finale between the Wild and Dallas Stars on Friday, Sept. 25. Faber wound up playing another 10 minutes before he left the game.

"He seemed okay," Guerin said. "As things progressed, we had to pull him."

He was placed on injured reserve retroactive to the injury. Standard injured reserve in the NHL mandates that a player miss a minimum of seven days from the date of the injury. Long-term injured reserve requires a player to miss at least 24 days or 10 games.

The Wild open the regular season Thursday night in Nashville.

articles.title: Reds star Elly De La Cruz earns another MLB honor after 30-30 season
articles.summary: "He's more special than I thought," teammate Eugenio Suárez said of Cincinnati Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz, the NL Player of the Month.
articles.body:
The individual hardware kept coming for the Cincinnati Reds even after the season , defying their last-place finish in the NL Central.

Shortstop Elly De La Cruz , who finished off the fourth 30-30 season in franchise history over the weekend in Toronto , won National League Player of the Month honors for September.

He hit .348 with nine home runs, six stolen bases and a 1.156 OPS, playing in all 24 of the Reds games in September.

Elly De La Cruz on verge of newest 30-30 season in Reds history

He's the second Red to win a player of the month award this season, joining outfielder JJ Bleday (May).

And first baseman Sal Stewart earned NL Rookie of the Month awards for both March/April and August – nabbing a player of the week award along the way.

De La Cruz, who was already off to a good start when he missed three weeks in June because of a hamstring injury, was one of the top performers in baseball after the injury.

Over his final 80 games, he hit .294 with 18 homers, 20 stolen bases, a .385 on-base percentage and .929 OPS.

He ranked second only to presumptive MVP Pete Crow-Armstrong of the Cubs in fangraphs.com WAR in that span.

Teammate Eugenio Suárez calls De La Cruz a "top three" player in baseball, "for real," after seeing up close every day for a season after only playing a few games a season against him in recent years.

"He's more special than I thought," Suárez said. "And he wants more. Almost every day he told me, 'I want more, I want more, I want more.'

"And he knows how to use his tools now."

Suárez described a more mature, focused player who quickly fixes mistakes and has learned to take walks.

"When you see that, you see the superstar," Suárez said. "He was a star. But now he's on top of the league."

After hitting his 30th home run of the season in Atlanta on Sept. 24, De La Cruz stole third base the next night in Toronto for his 30th steal to join mentors Eric Davis and Barry Larkin, along with Brandon Phillips as the only Reds to pull off a 30-30 season.

De La Cruz, a switch-hitter who's still just 24, focused during the offseason and in spring training on improving from the right side of the plate and made a stunning leap in performance – hitting .329 as a right-handed hitter with 11 homers and a 1.1014 OPS in 189 plate appearances.

But when asked where he thinks he improved the most, he didn't single out any area of his game.

"I think every part," he said. "And for next season I'm just going to keep working hard and getting better, and doing the little details."

articles.title: Rangers European prospects update: Mikkel Eriksen joins new team on loan
articles.summary: Across the pond, the New York Rangers have six prospects playing in Europe. And since our last update, there’ve been […]
articles.body:
Across the pond, the New York Rangers have six prospects playing in Europe. And since our last update, there've been some changes to note.

As discussed last week, Mikkel Eriksen was loaned to Mora IK in Allsvenskan, the second tier of professional hockey in Sweden. Across the border, Samuel Jung made his return in Finland after missing six weeks with an injury.

Let's get into the latest with the Rangers prospects playing in Europe.

CSKA Moscow, one of the biggest, most successful clubs in Russian hockey, is on a five-game winning streak. This past week they played three games, but Rangers prospect Ivan Patrikhayev only appeared in Wednesday's 2-0 win over Amur Khaborovsk. The 20-year-old defenseman was a healthy scratch for the games on Monday and Friday. Patrikhayev, who signed an extension through the 2027-28 season with the Moscow-based team, recorded a shot on goal in his only game last week, when he logged 13:46 TOI on the third defense pair.

It's worth noting that only eight defensemen aged 20 or younger have played more games this season in the KHL. Patrikhayev and 19-year-old Ivan Yukin share the work-load on the third pair for a loaded defensive corps. Yukin, undrafted, played in the games Monday and Friday for a combined 24 minutes and 49 seconds over two games.

Upcoming schedule: Tuesday against SKA St. Petersburg and Thursday against Dinamo Minsk

Rico Gredig played two games this week, and recorded his first point. After his move from HC Davos to EV Zug, the 2024 sixth-round pick appeared in all four of his new team's games. On Tuesday, Gredig took an early penalty that led to the game's first goal on the ensuing powerplay. He was overall quiet offensively, but early in the second period, Gredig took a high stick to the face and drew a double-minor penalty since he was bleeding. Zug was unfortunately not able to capitalize on the extended man advantage.

On Friday, the 21-year-old forward recorded his first point, an assist on the first goal of the game. Gredig skated the puck up the ice creating an odd-man rush, that led to the goal by Chris Egli. Unfortunately, it was not enough as Zug lost 5-3 and Gredig finished the game with a minus-1 rating in 14:02 TOI.

Upcoming schedule: Tuesday against SC Rapperswil-Jona Lakers and Thursday against Genève-Servette HC

Over in Slovakia, the reigning champions HK Nitra are off to a very poor start, with a 1-3-1 record after five games. Tomáš Chrenko has just one assist in those five games, a surprise after his strong showing for the Rangers in the Rookie Series against Philadelphia Flyers prospects.

In the showdown Friday against second-place Vlci Zilina, Chrenko's team picked up its first win of the season, a 3-1 triumph. Despite not recording any points, Chrenko had four shots on goal in just under 13 minutes of ice-time, his lowest of the season so far.

On Sunday, the 18-year-old forward recorded his first point of the season with an assist on the final goal of the game in a 4-2 loss. With 16 minutes and 35 seconds of ice-time, Chrenko was back in a more familiar role. The loss saw HK Nitra drop to 10th in the league, out of 12 teams.

Upcoming schedule: Tuesday against HK 32 Liptovsky Mikulas and Friday against Dukla Michalovce

Samuel Jung – KalPa Hockey (Liiga/SM Sarja)

Good news out of Finland, where Jung, the Czech winger, is back in game action. The 20-year-old who was selected in the sixth round in the 2025 draft, moved from Kärpät in Oulu, the third northernmost city in the world with a population of just over 100,000, down south to KalPa in Kuopio. During the preseason, Jung was injured when hit into the boards by Victor Lööf. He was out with an unspecified injury until this past week.

KalPa eased Jung back by having him play for their under-20 team on Saturday, when they took on HPK from Hämeenlinna. In a thrilling battle, the game went to overtime with a 5-5 score, and that's when Jung scored the winner. It was his fifth shot on goal, and this one finally found the back of the net. He finished with 19:23 TOI, second most by a forward, in his season debut.

Upcoming schedule: Thursday against SaiPa u20 and Friday against KooKoo u20

Mikkel Eriksen – Mora IK (HockeyAllsvenskan)

A week ago, it was announced that Rangers prospect Eriksen, a fourth round selection in the 2025 NHL Draft, was loaned out by his club Färjestad BK. His new team, Mora IK, is a familiar one to the 19-year old Norwegian center, since he spent time there last season on loan as well. His new club plays hockey in Allsvenskan, the second tier of Swedish hockey. It is very common for young players to be loaned out, often on short-term deals, to get playing time. Sweden's system is promotion-relegation, so the two leagues are a lot closer than the major vs minor league system in North America.

Since his arrival, Eriksen appeared in all three games, and centered the second line. He made his season debut on Wednesday in a 3-2 shootout loss to MoDo Hockey. He played 14 and 17 minutes in the following two games. Despite not recording any points, it is worth pointing out that his line did produce three goals last week, one of which coming from former Rangers prospect Oliver Tärnström. He was 12-for-27 on face-offs, struggling a bit on the draw against tougher and bigger opponents.

Upcoming schedule: Wednesday against Nybro Vikings IF and Friday against Kalmar HC

Rasmus Larsson – Hudiksvalls HC (HockeyEttan)

The final prospect to cover is a player who's been in the Rangers organization for three years, but has not been able to really raise expectations. Rasmus Larsson was picked in the fifth round of the 2023 NHL Draft. After a year in the USHL with the Green Bay Gamblers, followed by a freshman year in college with Northern Michigan, Larsson transferred to Robert Morris University ahead of the 2025-26 season, and this past summer decided to go back to Sweden.

The team he plays for, Hudiksvalls HC, finished first in HockeyEttan last season, the third tier of Swedish hockey. Teams can be promoted into the second tier HockeyAllsvenskan, but it's a hard barrier to cross. At this level, the 22-year old left-handed defenseman made his season debut on Saturday, and he scored a goal to go along with three shots in a 7-1 win. Sunday, his team won in a shootout for a 2-1 victory.

Upcoming schedule: Friday against Norrtälje IK

articles.title: Pistons get new offensive identity with improved shooting, floor spacing
articles.summary: With improved shooting from new players, the Pistons are expected to develop a new offensive identity in the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
DETROIT — Cade Cunningham organized a player-led minicamp for his teammates this summer. When he arrived at a San Diego gym in late August, Cunningham was excited about the turnout.

Almost every player on the roster attended the camp, except for Jalen Duren . His absence did not surprise Cunningham, given that the All-Star duo has been in contact all summer. The ongoing communication stems not only from the close relationship they have built over the years but also from Cunningham's understanding of what Duren is experiencing in his ongoing contract negotiations with the Detroit Pistons .

"He talked to me beforehand, and we were all good," Cunningham said during media day on Monday. "That's my brother, on and off the court. We have gone to war with each other. The negotiations are between him and the front office. That has nothing to do with me. The best thing I can do is support and encourage him, and try not to let him get too down."

Instead of focusing on Duren's absence, Cunningham focused on his teammates in San Diego. The minicamp gave the Pistons an early chance to build chemistry and prepare for the upcoming 2026-27 season. Two months later, Cunningham's approach foreshadowed how the Pistons began training camp on Tuesday at the Henry Ford Pistons Performance Center without their All-Star and All-NBA center, who remains out amid a contract dispute.

"You just have to coach the team. That decision is out of my hands right now, and I can't let it take away from my responsibility to the guys who are here," coach J.B. Bickerstaff said. "We prepare ourselves as coaches to put our best foot forward to give these guys who are in the gym now the best that we have, helping them prepare for how we move forward and getting us ready for the season."

The Pistons' training camp roster will include 19 players, a handful of which will highlight the significant changes the team made over the summer. Ausar Thompson recently had a moment of realization in the locker room at Little Caesars Arena, where he and Cunningham recognized that they were the only two players remaining from the team's abysmal 14-win season during the 2023-24 campaign.

Detroit parted ways with Tobias Harris , Isaiah Stewart and Marcus Sasser — three players who played prominent roles in Detroit's resurgence over the last two years. They replaced them with John Collins , Isaiah Joe and Taurean Prince — three players the Pistons believe will address the shortcomings that led to their second-round elimination by the Cleveland Cavaliers last season.

Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon believes each new addition can meet the team's defensive standard while also giving Bickerstaff more optionality and versatility in the rotation. However, each newcomer's biggest contribution to Detroit will be improving its shooting.

"I think we can still be a top defense in the league," Langdon said. "If I can keep that foundation, along with adding more shooting and more spacing, and cutting our turnovers down, that was the goal and the vision when it came to putting this team together. I do believe we have gotten better, but only time will tell."

Last season, Collins, Joe and Prince all shot 40.0% or better from beyond the arc for their respective teams. This will help the Pistons improve on their 17th-place finish last season, when they shot 35.6% from beyond the arc. Despite being mediocre from deep, the Pistons maintained one of the league's best offenses. They finished the season with the ninth-best offensive rating, posting a net rating of 117.3 while averaging 117.8 points per game.

The Pistons once believed they could succeed without strong 3-point shooting, but that strategy hurt their offense in the playoffs. They shot 35.9% from beyond the arc over 14 playoff games, which contributed to a drop in their offensive net rating to 110.4, while their scoring average fell to 104.9 points per game.

Building on last season's performance, the Pistons are optimistic that their improved shooting will help them establish a new offensive identity. The additions of Collins, Joe and Prince will not only improve Detroit's subpar 3-point shooting, but also create more space on the floor, requiring opponents to be mindful of their position on the court.

"The shooting is going to be a big difference for us," Bickerstaff said. "When you have guys who have proven in this league that they can carry weight and carry gravity, people are gonna have to play us differently. Also, these are guys who have been there before. Their experience, along with their skill set, will help. ...Their ability to move off the ball. It will make teams chase us instead of just sitting and packing the paint. All of those things will be helpful for us."

During their five-on-five sessions in Southern California, Cunningham noticed that each newcomer's shooting skills will not only impact the team's overall 3-point production, but also from an individual standpoint. Cunningham noted that his new teammates' shooting has created more one-on-one scoring opportunities because of the defensive pressure they generate. Thompson — a secondary ball-handler — agreed with Cunningham's observation.

"They are all knockdown shooters. I've been playing with them, and they have been very impressive," Thompson said. "I am super excited. The paint is going to be more open. I wish someone would step off one of them."

articles.title: Former Celt makes major Celtic and Martin O’Neill ‘standoff’ claim
articles.summary: Former Celtic defender Charlie Mulgrew has described what he believes to be a ‘standoff’ between Martin O’Neill and the Celtic board…Martin O’Neill, Manager...
articles.body:
Former Celtic defender Charlie Mulgrew has described what he believes to be a 'standoff' between Martin O'Neill and the Celtic board…

Martin O'Neill, Manager of Celtic, arrives at the stadium before the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and the Rangers at Celtic Park on September 20, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

Martin's position is now being questioned due to the recent run of three consecutive defeats, but he's expected to stay and battle through the current crisis.

But Mulgrew reckons that there's an obvious explanation for the veteran Irishman digging his heels and refusing to bow to the pressure.

Martin O'Neill should maybe have just rode off into the sunset

On The Breakdown podcast Mulgrew explained: "A lot of Celtic fans that I'm meeting are saying that Martin O'Neill should maybe have just rode off into the sunset after Celtic won the double.

"My take on that is that's fair enough. But my opinion is Martin O'Neill would have liked to have done that but – like we all would – his reward would have been a contract. A two-year contract, worth X amount.

Martin O'Neill, Manager of Celtic reacts during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Celtic FC and Ferencvarosi TC at Celtic Park on September 17, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

"If he just walks away and says 'thanks', I don't think he is getting a penny – or he is getting very little – compared to what he is due now. If they got rid of him now, it would be close to £1million I would imagine.

Mulgrew continued: "I think the standoff now is he still thinks he can do the job, but I don't think Martin O'Neill is leaving with no money. And I don't think Celtic want to pay him.

"Things aren't a disaster right now, he has only lost three games – three big games, and that is a disaster at Celtic sometimes – but if you actually take a step back, he is still top of the league.

Celtic manager Martin O'Neill and assistant Shaun Maloney during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD1 match between Celtic FC and Ferencvarosi TC at Celtic Park on September 17, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

"There is still a lot that can be done this season, there is a double still. If there is one man that can do it, it is him.

"So my point is, I think he would have liked to have done that [left in the summer] , but how do you go and knock back a two-year contract at Celtic with that money regardless of what age you are?"

Michael Nicholson stated that the club would back MON

After the defeat to the Rangers at Celtic Park, Martin admitted that he'd take a few days away with his family and would consider his position. Since then the Celtic support has had no real update other than Michael Nicholson's written remarks in the Celtic PLC Financial Results where we stated that the club would continue to support the manager.

So that rules out – for now at least – Celtic sacking Martin O'Neill. That would be unthinkable to most Celtic supporters with the more cynical ones pointing out that if Martin himself calls it a day he will NOT be entitled to the value of his one year contract, or what's left of it.

Martin O'Neill arrives at the stadium. Celtic v Rangers. Scottish Premiership. 20 September 2026. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

Both parties have an option for a second year but around the time of his recent health scare that he would definitely NOT look to take up that option himself, so we are essentially talking about ten months salary.

Celtic's next three fixtures are far from being easy

If Martin wants to go but can't for financial reasons then that is appalling. Celtic's next three fixtures are far from being easy. Motherwell away is followed by a trip to Lisbon to take on high flying Benfica then it's a tasty match against Hearts at Celtic Park.

Martin O'Neill arrives at Ibrox. Rangers v Celtic, Premier Sports Cup quarter final. Sunday 13 September 2026. Photo Vagelis Georgariou

Few would bet on Celtic winning all three of those games, unfortunately.

Speculation around Martin's future will intensify the longer this goes on with no real update. And you are left wondering what is happening at Lennoxtown during this international break regarding tactics and finding a solution to Celtic midfield woes.

Let's be honest Celtic are unlikely to get anything in Lisbon

Martin did say that the non international players would get much of last week off but would be back at Lennoxtown this week. Presumably he would have been there too but we don't know.

Let's be honest Celtic are unlikely to get anything in Lisbon – it would be a major surprise if that wasn't the case. If we lose at Fir Park before that game we could be in a position of having lost five matches on the bounce.

It's a real mess that has the potential to turn into a crisis and this time a managerial change that will involve paying a club legend what he is due. Let's hope that there's a solution on the park at Motherwell that relieves the pressure.
