articles.title: Lakers try to move forward but specter of LeBron James remains topic at media day
articles.summary: From Rob Pelinka through Luka Doncic and Bronny James, the team is ready to turn the page.
articles.body:
"Clearly, new team, new players, and that's what we're going to talk about today," was the tone Rob Pelinka, the Lakers ' head of basketball operations, tried to set for the franchise in a press conference last week. "We just, as an organization, are so grateful for the run that we had with [ LeBron James ] here... it was a great era, and we're grateful for it. So I just think it's important to say that at the onset as we turn into a new chapter."

The Los Angeles Lakers are ready to move on from the LeBron James era — an eight-season run that brought them a title and made them a perennial playoff team — to what comes next, a team better built to maximize Luka Doncic . Yet the ghost of LeBron still seemed to haunt Lakers media day despite the fact that he was 2,400 miles away in a different uniform .

When Doncic talked to ESPN's Brian Windhorst, LeBron leaving came up. Of course.

"It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him... We all know who LeBron James is."

Doncic, for his part, spent much of the day trying to spin things forward, this was part of his ESPN interviews .

"I'm really excited about this team. I think we have a lot of underrated guys. There are some guys that came in that are not talked about a lot, but I really enjoy them and I really like what I see."

Nobody faced more of that than Bronny James , LeBron James' son, who remains in Los Angeles for his third season and should see more regular minutes this season, potentially even cracking the regular rotation.

"You guys know me as Bronny. My real name is LeBron," Bronny said from the podium. "I've been doing this for however long, so I think it's a motivating factor for me just getting up every day and trying to prove myself as Bronny instead of LeBron...

"That's my dad. I spent 22 years almost with him, so, just another experience that I'm going to be a part of. I'm excited for how it's going to feel during the season, too. Looking forward to it."

One void to fill without LeBron is leadership — he commanded the locker room and was the team's unquestioned leader. Now, Doncic and the newly signed Austin Reaves will fill that role together. Lakers forward Jake LaRavia said from the podium it would be no problem for Doncic and Reaves to share the role.

"They get along so well that it's kind of easy for them to co-lead this team. I think sometimes Luka leads by example and we watch him and we watch how he goes about himself. AR can sometimes be a bit more vocal. But I think they both do a great job at what they are good at it when it comes to being leaders for this team."

As long as Doncic stays healthy, the Lakers are going to be good. How good depends on how Walker Kessler steps up into the role of starting center on the Lakers, plus how well role players like Quentin Grimes , LaRavia, Sandro Mamukelashvili , Collin Sexton , Ziaire Williams and others can deliver on both ends of the court.

If they do, the questions about LeBron will stop. Or, at least, slow down.

articles.title: Injury-plagued Panthers suffer big loss with G Damien Lewis sidelined
articles.summary: Carolina's top offensive lineman in last week's game suffered a UCL injury with no clear return timetable.
articles.body:
Diving to recover Carolina Panthers running back Chuba Hubbard 's fumble on a 2-point conversion attempt last Sunday, guard Damien Lewis reached out in vain.

The seven-year veteran failed to secure the loose ball and ended up re-aggravating his ailing elbow, remaining on the Huntington Bank Field for medical treatment for the second time. Lewis also sustained an injury that kept him out for most of the second quarter.

Lewis returned both times during the Panthers' 21-18 loss to the blitz-heavy Cleveland Browns , but he could be lost for several weeks with a UCL injury in his elbow, as reported by @MikeGarafolo and @RapSheet .

Despite subpar performances by the other four offensive line starters, Lewis held up against the Browns' pressure, earning the Panthers' highest offensive grade (89.7), according to Pro Football Focus. He was the lone offensive lineman not to yield pressure.

Guard Robert Hunt and tackles Rasheed Walker and Monroe Freeling each surrendered six pressures and center Luke Fortner received the unit's lowest pass-blocking grade (34.4).

When the Panthers released their Week 1 depth chart, Lewis, who also suffered a lower-body injury in the regular-season opening loss, was the lone listed left guard.

Panthers G Damien Lewis out for foreseeable future

With the Detroit Lions (2-1) scheduled for a primetime matchup Sunday night at Bank of America Stadium, Panthers offensive line coach Joe Gilbert likely will prep Corey Bullock , who replaced Lewis during the second quarter against the Browns.

The Panthers (1-2) claimed Bullock off waivers from the Baltimore Ravens following cutdown day. A 2024 undrafted free agent appeared in 16 games last season and could be in line for his first NFL start.

He could be challenged to replace Lewis, who allowed one sack and 13 pressures during 553 pass-blocking snaps last season. He will undoubtedly be challenged by a Lions defense that may follow the Browns' lead and continue pressuring Panthers quarterback Bryce Young .

In a copycat league, the Panthers' offensive front should expect to see a variety of blitz packages from opposing defenses. Young, who leads the NFL with 939 passing yards, endured pressure on 32 of his 51 dropbacks against the Browns.

Will it become an early-season blueprint?

"We didn't handle the movement well up front, and we're looking at it schematically and structurally the runs looked fine," Canales said, per Panthers.com . "We missed some blocks up front. Some of (the Browns') rush patterns (were) creating a little bit of pressure for Bryce."

The pressure is building on the Panthers' medical staff.

Along with Lewis , key contributors Jalen Coker (quad strain), Jaycee Horn (torn quad), Mike Jackson (groin), Xavier Legette (knee), Devin Lloyd (knee) and Nick Scott (rib) remain hobbled. The Panthers will release the week's first injury report Wednesday.

"There's no replacing Jaycee Horn," Canales said. "We're not asking our guys to replace Jaycee. We're just asking them to do their job."

That MASH list does not include projected starting tackles Taylor Moton (blood clots) and Ikem Ekwonu (knee), who have yet to dress this season but could return after the Week 5 bye, RB2 Jonathon Brooks , or reserve OL Brady Christensen (hamstring) or special teams aces Claudin Cherelus (shoulder) and Bam Martin-Scott (hamstring).

As local tabloid The Express understands, 1.FC Köln is apparently preparing for a sudden and unexpected change of coach.

It's believed Köln held a "meeting of the Joint Committee" where, among other things, the future of René Wagner was discussed.

Resulting from the discussion, should Köln lose to local rivals Borussia Mönchengladbach on 11 October, Wagner could be sacked.

Furthermore, the Bundesliga club is reportedly already in agreement with a potential successor in the form of Horst Steffen.

The 57-year-old was most recently in charge of Werder Bremen until February 2026, has since been linked with numerous clubs.

Steffen was reportedly at the Geißbockheim on Saturday to watch Köln's reserves defeat VfB Hilden – and possibly to hold negotiations.

Under Wagner, who initially took over the role on an interim basis, Effzeh have only managed two wins in his eleven league matches to date.

Against Borussia Mönchengladbach, Wagner apparently needs points to win back the support of the club's management.

articles.title: Steelers Week 3 grades in win over Bengals
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers Week 3 grades.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers did a complete 180 from their performance in Week 2 and saw their offense come to life against the Cincinnati Bengals in a 30-27 win. As they get ready for the Cleveland Browns on a short week, we give you our Week 3 grades as the Steelers improved to 2-1.

​ Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers looked as good as he ever has in a Steelers uniform. He finished the week tied for eighth in EPA per play among quarterbacks, and nearly topped 300 yards with three touchdowns. Had a pass not bounced off Roman Wilson 's hands for an interception, his stat line would have been as close to perfect as it can get. Great bounce back from Rodgers and the offense. Grade: A

Joey Bray: Was it the cleanest game from Aaron Rodgers? No, but it was easily one of the better performances we have ever seen from the veteran quarterback in a Steelers uniform. Again, Rodgers was let down by his receivers, who left a few completions on the field. Despite all of the miscommunications and trouble snapping the ball on time, Rodgers threw for nearly 300 yards and three touchdowns. This is the type of performance you should be hoping for every week from your 42-year-old quarterback. Grade: A

​ Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers had over 400 yards of offense on Sunday, and that was in no small part due to the upgraded play on the offensive line. Brock Hoffman and Max Iheanachor made their respective first starts of the season, and instantly provided more time for Rodgers to throw and opened more lanes for Jaylen Warren to run through. While we can't expect them to be perfect each week, this was as close to perfection as it gets. Grade: A+

Joey Bray : It cannot be overstated just how much the offensive line play opened up the Steelers offense in Week 3. Rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor got his first career start at right tackle, while veteran Brock Hoffman took over for Spencer Anderson at right guard. Both played well, and you could see the difference in the offense this week. Both the running and passing game both saw season highs in terms of production while the offense scored 30 points after scoring just 16 points through the first two weeks. While it's still hard to imagine we see the offense put up 30 points every week, the changes to the offensive line seem to have made a massive impact on the offense. Grade: A+

​ Jarrett Bailey: Warren had a career day, putting up a career-best 176 yards from scrimmage. Had his run of north of 80 yards not been taken away due to a ticky-tack penalty, we could be talking about Warren topping 200 yards on the ground. Keep feeding No. 30. Grade: A

Joey Bray : This was one of the very best games that Jaylen Warren has played in the NFL. Warren averaged 7.5 yards per carry and had an 84-yard run negated due to a holding call. He also should have at least ten more yards and a touchdown to his total if he weren't caught by the turf monster. The speedy back had to carry the load with the absence of Ric Dowdle, and proved that he deserves a larger slice of the pie even when Dowdle is back healthy. Grade: A+

Jarrett Bailey: It's constantly one step forward and another step back for Wilson. He was sprung open for a touchdown on the opening drive, and then had a pass bounce off his hands for an interception later on in the game. Germie Bernard needs more looks. Grade: C+

Joey Bray : Man, I really thought I was going to be able to talk nicely about Roman Wilson after his 38-yard touchdown on the opening drive of the game. However, Wilson is responsible for Rodgers' interception as the ball bounced right off the hands of the young receiver. Wilson was left on the bench for a good majority of the second half as rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard saw the field more. The inconsistencies of Wilson continue to outshine any bright spot he creates. He continues to be a frustrating player to evaluate. Grade: C

​ Jarrett Bailey: I'm not going to crush the Steelers' secondary. When you face an elite quarterback and two high-caliber receivers, you're going to give up yards. Burrow was getting the ball out quickly, and both Chase and Higgins had good days picking apart the consistent zone looks from the Steelers. They need to be better as a unit, but it also felt like the plan was to be a bend don't break defense against an elite passing attack. Grade: C

Joey Bray : I have a tough time being super hard on the secondary considering they are down two of their best players in Joey Porter Jr. and DeShon Elliott . That being said, this was their worst showing of the season. Joe Burrow started the game 14/14 and had a solid game overall. The Bengals, of course, have one of the best receiver duos in the league, which poses its own set of challenges for the Steelers each time they play Cincinnati. It was another zone coverage-heavy game for the defense who was picked apart by an elite quarter and a duo of elite receivers. Grade: D

​Jarrett Bailey: Sunday felt like a vintage Steelers win, largely due to their luck and playmaking on special teams. A roughing the kicker call on Cam Johnston extended a drive that led to a DK Metcalf touchdown. A muffed punt was then recovered by Ben Skowronek and set up a Chris Boswell field goal, of which he went 3-for-3 on the day. A great day for the special teams. Grade: A

Joey Bray : After missing a field goal in each of the first two games, Chris Boswell went 3-for-3 on field goals. Cam Johnston appeared to get hit during a punt but bounced back and turned in a solid performance. Kaden Wetjen has yet to make any impact plays as a return man, but it could only be a matter of time before he breaks one loose. Grade: A

Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more!

articles.title: Why America East coaches may be underrating Bryant women this season
articles.summary: The Bulldogs are picked fifth in the preseason poll despite returning two all-conference players and adding some impact transfers.
articles.body:
Will a core trio be enough of a foundation for Bryant to contend in this year's America East women's basketball title race?

Opposing coaches still think the Bulldogs could need more help. They were picked fifth in the preseason poll released Monday, Sept. 28, despite boasting two of the top six players in the league.

Mia Mancini and Nia Scott were among the all-conference selections, veterans in the backcourt and frontcourt, respectively. Martina Boba will serve as a team captain alongside her fellow seniors, as Bryant will attempt to look more like the team that started 2025-26 instead of the club that scuffled to the finish.

"I think it speaks volumes to have three seniors who have been here all four years," Bryant coach Lynne-Ann Kokoski said on a live broadcast with The Field of 68. "They understand. They've been through the good, the bad and the ugly – the rebuilding and, hopefully, propelling this program forward.

"Those guys understand what it takes and what we need to do to get there, which is tremendous."

Mancini has been a standout since claiming league Rookie of the Year honors in her 2023-24 debut. The former star at the Wheeler School was among the leaders for the Bulldogs in scoring, rebounding, assists and steals per game. Mancini added 59 made 3-pointers to close inside the conference's top five.

"She's done a lot of great things for us in her four years here," Kokoski said. "I think one of the biggest steps for her is being a more vocal leader, and we've seen that."

Scott has been a constant double-double threat in the paint for Bryant, racking up 11 of those in 2025-26. She averaged 11.8 points, 8.7 rebounds and shot 53% from the floor last season. Scott intends to expand her game to the perimeter this season, adding an outside shot to her strong post presence.

Take a look: Bryant women's basketball rolls over UMass Lowell, 77-36

"I think you'll see a lot more versatility," Kokoski said. "We just don't have traditional posts anymore."

Boba's defensive ability and toughness mixes with what could be a deep lineup bolstered by transfer talent. Genevive Wedemeyer (Siena), Ndate Ndiaye (Florida International) and Cameron McNamara (Highland Community College) are all expected to make immediate impacts alongside rotation returners Izzy Adams and Olivia Fernandez.

"I want those guys to be impact players," Kokoski said. "Honestly, I think the hardest part for them right now is understanding. Go step on toes."

The Bulldogs closed 18-12 overall and 8-8 in league play last season. Their highlights all came early – a win over Boston College, a 14-3 start overall, a 4-0 beginning in league play. Bryant struggled down the stretch and lost to Binghamton in a quarterfinal stinker, a 45-44 setback on the road.

"Just keep building," Kokoski said. "Obviously the goal is always to get to 20 (wins). The goal is always to finish top four. The goal is always to win a championship. But you can't do that until you lay that foundation."

The Bearcats grabbed six first-place votes to top the poll while Maryland Baltimore County earned two and Vermont picked up one. Maine was selected fourth ahead of the Bulldogs while New Jersey Institute of Technology, Albany, New Hampshire and UMass Lowell occupied the last four spots.

Binghamton matched Bryant with two players on the all-conference list. Seniors Bella Pucci and Kendall Bennett give the Bearcats a premier outside-inside punch as a leading scorer and dominant rebounder. Catamounts guard Malia Lenz and Retrievers guard Heidi Williams rounded out the players tabbed to be among the league's best this season. Lenz piled up 13 points and 14 rebounds as Vermont beat the Black Bears in the conference tournament championship game and booked a trip to the NCAA Tournament.

The Bulldogs open with a Division III opponent on Nov. 2, hosting MIT. Bryant follows with a home game against Marist before jumping into the teeth of its schedule – at Providence, at Boston College and a Dec. 21 home game against Brown all follow. A trip to face the Wildcats on New Year's Eve starts to conference schedule, a 4 p.m. tip in New Hampshire.

articles.summary: Manchester City say they are ‘disappointed and surprised’ by the verdict and will appeal.
articles.body:
Manchester City have been found guilty of ⁠all charges ⁠of serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules between the 2009/10 and 2017/18 seasons, the league has said in ⁠a statement.

City were charged in February 2023 with breaches of the league’s financial rules spanning nine seasons following ⁠a four-year investigation.

The club said in a statement it would appeal “on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe”.

An independent commission found that City “arranged ‘sham’ contracts (which ‌misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners,” the league said on Tuesday.

The league added that the commission had found City used schemes “to artificially inflate the club’s revenues, and reduce its costs, by more than 900 million pounds during the affected period, to appear to comply with financial rules.”

“The ⁠core decision … details how the club systematically ⁠broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade,” said Richard Masters, the chief executive of the Premier League.

“There are elements of the case that remain to be ⁠decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches.”

City, who deny any wrongdoing, said ⁠they were “disappointed and surprised” by the ⁠commission’s opinion.

“The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its ‌positions, relating to this case,” the club said.

“Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the ‌basis ‌that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.”
